title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
皇上臨御之五年壬子天下當開
科取士湖廣藩臬諸臣協謀
於巡按監察御史汪宗器預
期聘曉等以司文衡顧貢院
湫隘為之闢而新之時巡撫
右副都御史謝綬撫治右副
===
都御史王道清戎監察御史
梁廷賓祇若
德意惇尚文教而鎮守太監劉
雅分守太監韋貴潘記總兵
官鎮遠侯顧溥又協德賛襄
士風丕振至期左布政使劉
喬左參政李琮副使俞振才
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

皇上臨御之五年壬子，天下當開科取士。湖廣藩臬諸臣協謀於巡按監察御史汪宗器，預期聘曉等以司文衡。顧貢院湫隘，為之闢而新之。時巡撫右副都御史謝綬、撫治右副都御史王道、清戎監察御史梁廷賓，祇若德意，惇尚文教，而鎮守太監劉雅、分守太監韋貴、潘記、總兵官鎮遠侯顧溥，又協德賛襄，士風丕振。至期，左布政使劉喬、左參政李琮、副使俞振才
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the fifth year of His Majesty’s reign, the renzi year (1492), examinations were due to be held throughout the empire to select men of talent. The officials of Huguang’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions consulted with the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Wang Zongqi, and engaged Xiao and others in advance to serve as examiners. Finding the examination compound low-lying and cramped, they expanded and renovated it. At that time, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Xie Shou, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Dao, charged with pacification, and Investigating Censor Liang Tingbin, charged with inspecting military affairs, reverently followed the imperial intentions and earnestly promoted literary education. The eunuch Director serving as Defender, Liu Ya; the eunuch Directors serving as Area Defenders, Wei Gui and Pan Ji; and the Regional Commander, Gu Pu, Marquis of Zhenyuan, likewise worked together in support. The spirit of the scholars was greatly invigorated. When the appointed time arrived, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Liu Qiao, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Li Cong, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Yu Zhencai…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
吳欽則提調監試於内右布
政使王範右參政劉聰副使
鄭恭陳孜王玹左右參議章
玄應李俊馬銓鄭觀僉事馮
鎮戚昂張賓馬璠冨玹陳璉
則綜理防範於外御史汪宗
器寔監臨焉凡諸執事皆遴
===
選以克期得真才用圖報稱
合提學副使焦芳所簡拔士
凡一千五百有竒三試之得
其尤者八十五人將錄其名
拜文以
獻曉當序其端嘗聞之先民有
言曰山川之秀麗必有俊傑
punctuated: 吳欽則提調監試於内，右布政使王範、右參政劉聰、副使鄭恭、陳孜、王玹、左右參議章玄應、李俊、馬銓、鄭觀、僉事馮鎮、戚昂、張賓、馬璠、冨玹、陳璉則綜理防範於外，御史汪宗器寔監臨焉。凡諸執事皆遴選，以克期得真才，用圖報稱。合提學副使焦芳所簡拔士，凡一千五百有竒，三試之，得其尤者八十五人。將錄其名，拜文以獻，曉當序其端。嘗聞之，先民有言曰：「山川之秀麗，必有俊傑
translation_en: …Wu Qin supervised arrangements and invigilated within, while Wang Fan, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Liu Cong, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Zheng Gong, Chen Zi, and Wang Xuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Zhang Xuanying, Li Jun, Ma Quan, and Zheng Guan, Left and Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners; and Feng Zhen, Qi Ang, Zhang Bin, Ma Fan, Fu Xuan, and Chen Lian, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners, coordinated administration and safeguards outside. Investigating Censor Wang Zongqi served as Supervising Official. All those undertaking duties were carefully selected, in the firm hope of obtaining truly talented men and thereby suitably repaying imperial favor. The candidates selected by Jiao Fang, Surveillance Vice Commissioner overseeing education, were assembled, numbering more than fifteen hundred in all. They were examined in three sessions, and eighty-five of the most outstanding were selected. Their names were to be recorded and their writings respectfully presented [?], and it fell to me, Xiao, to write the preface. I have heard a saying of the ancients: “Where mountains and rivers are beautiful, there must be outstanding men…”

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
居其間然而湖湘有荊衡太
和諸山有江漢洞庭諸水形
勝甲於天下徵之前時俊傑
之生于其間者固不可謂無
人亦未見其多也竊嘗疑之
今觀諸生塲屋所作詞粹理
完竒珎疊見而英焰奪目令
===
人顧接失次俊傑之士一何
多歟然嗇於前而豐於今蓋
嘗求其故矣湖湘土曠人稀
田者利沃饒漁者利瀦澤賈
者利丹銀齒革以是終其身
而遺其子孫焉其於禮樂文
章經綸仕進之心泊如也惟
punctuated: 居其間。」然而湖湘有荊衡、太和諸山，有江漢、洞庭諸水，形勝甲於天下。徵之前時，俊傑之生于其間者，固不可謂無人，亦未見其多也。竊嘗疑之。今觀諸生塲屋所作，詞粹理完，竒珎疊見，而英焰奪目，令人顧接失次。俊傑之士一何多歟！然嗇於前而豐於今，蓋嘗求其故矣。湖湘土曠人稀，田者利沃饒，漁者利瀦澤，賈者利丹銀齒革，以是終其身，而遺其子孫焉。其於禮樂文章、經綸仕進之心，泊如也。惟
translation_en:
…dwell among them.” Yet the Hu-Xiang region has such mountains as Jing, Heng, and Taihe, and such waters as the Jiang and Han rivers and Lake Dongting; its magnificent terrain ranks foremost under Heaven. Looking back to earlier times, one certainly cannot say that no outstanding men were born here, yet neither does it appear that they were numerous. I have privately often wondered about this. Now, examining what the candidates have written in the examination halls, I find their language refined and their reasoning complete. Rare treasures appear one after another, their brilliance dazzling the eyes, leaving one unable to attend to them in an orderly fashion. How numerous these outstanding scholars are! Why, then, were they scarce before and plentiful now? I have sought the reason.

The Hu-Xiang region has extensive lands and a sparse population. Farmers profit from its fertile soil, fishermen from its pools and marshes, and merchants from its cinnabar, silver, tusks, and hides. By these means they sustain themselves throughout their lives and leave a livelihood to their descendants. title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
我
列聖相承誕敷文教漸漬薰蒸多
歷年所然後俊傑往往抱藝
而出及我
聖天子在上鼓舞維新甄陶益至
則士類趨焉若流文風爲之
蔚然而無復狃於曩時之習
===
矣胡怪乎俊傑之多於今日
也哉嗚呼有此天地即有此
山川而俊傑之盛寔
聖朝重熙累洽氣化使然也山川
何預乎詩所謂維嶽降神生
甫及申亦乘有周氣化之盛
而生焉耳崧嶽奚功哉然人
punctuated:
我列聖相承，誕敷文教，漸漬薰蒸，多歷年所，然後俊傑往往抱藝而出。及我聖天子在上，鼓舞維新，甄陶益至，則士類趨焉若流，文風爲之蔚然，而無復狃於曩時之習矣。胡怪乎俊傑之多於今日也哉！
嗚呼！有此天地，即有此山川，而俊傑之盛，寔聖朝重熙累洽，氣化使然也。山川何預乎？《詩》所謂「維嶽降神，生甫及申」，亦乘有周氣化之盛而生焉耳，崧嶽奚功哉！然人
translation_en:
…our successive sage sovereigns have broadly spread cultural instruction. Through its gradual permeation and transforming influence over many years, outstanding men have at last repeatedly emerged, bringing their learning and accomplishments with them. Now that our sagely Son of Heaven reigns, inspiring renewal and nurturing talent with still greater care, scholars flock toward this endeavor like flowing water. Literary culture has consequently flourished, and they are no longer bound by the habits of former times. Why, then, should we wonder that outstanding men are so numerous today?
Alas! These mountains and rivers have existed as long as heaven and earth themselves, yet the abundance of outstanding men is truly the result of the transforming vital forces generated by our sagely dynasty’s successive ages of splendor and accumulated peace. What part do mountains and rivers play in this? As the Book of Odes says, “The sacred mountain sent down its divine power, giving birth to Fu and Shen.” They, too, were merely born amid the flourishing transformative forces of the Zhou. What credit can the lofty sacred mountain claim? Yet people…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
物固無預於山川而山川必
待人物而有名如隆中以武
侯名舂陵以茂叔名是也諸
生亦能如武侯茂叔以名山
川乎或曰子之論得矣但以
言而謂湖湘俊傑之多言果
足以定其人乎余曰言者心
===
之聲文又言之成章者也言
之在人猶水之瀾木之華也
泝源於瀾反本於華水木之
凡異可知已孟子曰我知言
言豈不可以知人乎雖然知
不知主薦者之責而俊傑之
實則被薦者之責諸生其以
punctuated: 物固無預於山川，而山川必待人物而有名，如隆中以武侯名、舂陵以茂叔名是也。諸生亦能如武侯、茂叔以名山川乎？或曰：「子之論得矣，但以言而謂湖湘俊傑之多，言果足以定其人乎？」余曰：「言者，心之聲；文又言之成章者也。言之在人，猶水之瀾、木之華也。泝源於瀾，反本於華，水木之凡異可知已。孟子曰：『我知言。』言豈不可以知人乎？雖然，知不知，主薦者之責；而俊傑之實，則被薦者之責。諸生其以
translation_en:
…people’s distinction indeed owes nothing to mountains and rivers, yet mountains and rivers must await distinguished people to become renowned. Thus Longzhong is renowned through Wuhou, the Marquis of Wu, and Chongling through Maoshu. Can you students likewise bring renown to mountains and rivers, as Wuhou and Maoshu did?
Someone said: “Your argument is sound. Yet you base your assertion that Huxiang has many outstanding talents solely on their words. Are words really sufficient to judge the people themselves?”
I replied: “Words are the voice of the heart, and literary compositions are words arranged into coherent patterns. Words in a person are like ripples on water or blossoms on a tree. Trace the ripples to their source and the blossoms back to their root, and you can tell whether the water and trees are ordinary or exceptional. Mengzi said: ‘I understand words.’ How, then, could words not enable us to understand people? Nevertheless, whether one recognizes talent is the responsibility of those charged with recommending candidates; actually possessing outstanding talent is the responsibility of those recommended. You students should take …

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
俊傑自待母使余失言也哉
福建延平府南平縣儒學教
諭梁曉謹序
punctuated:
俊傑自待，母使余失言也哉！
福建延平府南平縣儒學教諭梁曉謹序。
translation_en:
…hold yourselves to the standard of outstanding men, and do not let my words prove mistaken! [The transcription 母 is understood as 毋, “do not.”]
Preface respectfully written by Liang Xiao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Nanping County, Yanping Prefecture, Fujian.

第壹場

四書
知之爲知之，不知爲不知。

禹之行水也，行其所無事也。

易
龍德而正中者也。
節以制度，不傷財，不害民。
天之所助者，順也；人之所助者，信也。
舟楫之利，以濟不通。

書
象以典刑，流宥五刑，鞭作官刑，扑作教刑，金作贖刑。

王曰：「旨哉，說！乃言惟服。乃不良于言，予罔聞于行。」說拜稽首曰：「非知之艱，行之惟艱。」

First Session

Four Books
To acknowledge what you know as known, and what you do not know as unknown.
To have King Ji as one's father and King Wu as one's son.
When Yu guided the waters, he guided them along courses requiring no interference.

Book of Changes
One who possesses the dragon's virtue and is correctly situated in the center.
Restraint through regulations and measures neither depletes wealth nor harms the people.
Those whom Heaven assists are compliant; those whom people assist are trustworthy.
The usefulness of boats and oars lies in crossing otherwise impassable waters.

Book of Documents
He displayed the prescribed punishments, permitted exile in mitigation of the five punishments, made whipping the punishment for official misconduct and the rod the punishment in instruction, and allowed payment in metal to redeem punishment.
Eastward, it meets the Si and Yi rivers, and eastward enters the sea.
The king said: “Excellent, Yue! Your words must be put into practice. If you do not speak well, I shall hear nothing of your actions.” Yue bowed and knocked his head to the ground, saying: “It is not knowing that is difficult; putting knowledge into practice is difficult.”

八年
===

曹伯莒子杞伯同盟于蒲成公九年

采采芣苢，薄言采之；采采芣苢，薄言有之。
乃生男子，載寢之牀，載衣之裳，載弄之璋。
作邑于豐，文王烝哉！築城伊淢，作豐伊匹。匪棘其欲，遹追來孝。
如火烈烈，則莫我敢曷。

春秋

蕭叔朝公，莊公二十三年；公朝于王所，僖公二十八年。
宋公、楚子、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會于盂，執宋公以伐宋；楚人使宜申來獻捷，俱僖公二十一年。

translation_en:
Book of Odes

Luxuriant grows the plantain; let us gather it. Luxuriant grows the plantain; let us take it home.

When a son is born, lay him upon a bed, clothe him in robes, and give him a jade tablet to play with.

He established a city at Feng: how great was King Wen! He built its walls to accord with the moat and established Feng on a fitting scale. He did not hasten to fulfill his own desires, but carried forward the filial purposes of his forebears.

Like a fiercely blazing fire, none dares to stop us.

Spring and Autumn Annals

Shu of Xiao paid court to the duke—in the twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang. The duke paid court at the king’s residence—in the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.

The Duke of Song, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao met at Yu. They seized the Duke of Song and attacked Song. The men of Chu sent Yishen to present the spoils of victory. Both entries are from the twenty-first year of Duke Xi.

We took the fields of Wenyang—in the second year of Duke Cheng. The duke went to Jin—in the third year of Duke Cheng. The Marquis of Jin sent Han Chuan to convey instructions concerning the fields of Wenyang: they were to be returned to Qi—in the eighth year of Duke Cheng. The duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, and the Earl of Qi, and they jointly entered into a covenant at Pu—in the ninth year of Duke Cheng.

We entered Zhu and brought back Yi, Viscount of Zhu—in the seventh year of Duke Ai. The men of Qi took Huan and Chan. We returned Yi, Viscount of Zhu, to Zhu. The men of Qi returned Huan and Chan. These last entries are all from …

…the eighth year of Duke Ai. The duke joined Wu in attacking Qi: the tenth year of Duke Ai. Guo Shu of Qi led an army to attack us: the eleventh year of Duke Ai.

Book of Rites

The Minister of Education, Minister of War, and Minister of Works present the accomplishments of the hundred officials to the Son of Heaven for appraisal.

Virtue spreads forth, nurturing the myriad things; its ordering is extensive, and the things it embraces are abundant.

This is called supreme fittingness. Then the sages established the relationships of father and son, ruler and minister, to serve as the guiding framework. Once this framework was correctly established, all under Heaven became fully settled. Once all under Heaven was fully settled, they tuned the six pitch standards, harmonized the five notes, and sang the poems and hymns to string accompaniment. This is called the sound of virtue. The sound of virtue is called music.

The alternating singing is performed three times through, and the combined music is performed three times through.

Second Session

Discourse

A ruler of great accomplishment.

One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [the transcription 科 is doubtful].

Compose a draft edict in the voice of the Han emperor dispatching General Zhou Yafu and others to station troops in defense of the frontier: the sixth year of Emperor Wen.

Compose a draft Tang proclamation appointing Dai Zhou Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review: the first year of Zhenguan.

Compose a draft memorial of thanks in the voice of Sima Guang upon his appointment as a Hanlin Academician under the Song: the fourth year of Zhiping.

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
判語五條
增減官文書
立嫡子違法
僧道拜父母
主將不固守
告狀不受理
第叁場
策五道
問有非常之君必有非常之製作有至德
===
之行必有至德之文章典謨訓誥誓命
唐虞三代之製作文章善矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝條成
大誥三編
太宗文皇帝製為性理一書
宣宗章皇帝製為五倫一書殆與唐虞三代之
製作文章合轍而同符也伏讀
誥中所載有所謂君臣同遊申明五常者又
有所謂京民同樂斷指誹謗者與典謨

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所載有合者乎有所謂朝臣優劣知報
獲福者又有所謂居處僭分無作非爲
者與訓誥所載有同者乎
性理書備述先儒之言而叙周張於首矣然
而周張之所立者何言
五倫書昭示綱常之理而叙君臣於首矣然
而君臣之所重者何事其所立之言所
重之事抑與誓命諸篇有意指弗殊者
乎諸士子服膺
===
聖訓于兹有年其必知之悉矣試爲我言之
問自古有天下者未嘗不以
儲嗣爲重仰承
明詔建立
東宮誠足以固
邦本定名分安人心矣然賈誼嘗曰天下之
命繫于太子太子之善在於早諭教與
選左右教得而左右正則太子正而天
下定真確論也故太甲當幼冲之時師
punctuated:
所載有合者乎？有所謂「朝臣優劣」、「知報獲福」者，又有所謂「居處僭分」、「無作非爲」者，與訓誥所載有同者乎？《性理》書備述先儒之言，而叙周張於首矣，然而周張之所立者何言？《五倫》書昭示綱常之理，而叙君臣於首矣，然而君臣之所重者何事？其所立之言、所重之事，抑與誓命諸篇有意指弗殊者乎？諸士子服膺聖訓，于兹有年，其必知之悉矣，試爲我言之。

問：自古有天下者，未嘗不以儲嗣爲重。仰承明詔，建立東宮，誠足以固邦本、定名分、安人心矣。然賈誼嘗曰：「天下之命繫于太子，太子之善在於早諭教與選左右。教得而左右正，則太子正而天下定。」真確論也。故太甲當幼冲之時，師
translation_en:
…accord with what is recorded in the Canons and Counsels? There are also the sections entitled “The Merits and Faults of Court Officials” and “Knowing to Repay and Receiving Blessings,” as well as “Exceeding One’s Station in One’s Dwelling” and “Do Not Commit Wrongdoing.” Do these have anything in common with what is recorded in the Instructions and Announcements?

The book Nature and Principle (Xingli) comprehensively recounts the words of earlier Confucian scholars, placing Zhou Dunyi and Zhang Zai at the beginning. Yet what teachings did Zhou and Zhang establish? The book The Five Human Relationships (Wulun) clearly sets forth the principles of the cardinal relationships and constant virtues, placing ruler and minister first. Yet what matters are most important in the relationship between ruler and minister? Might the teachings established by those scholars and the matters emphasized in this relationship be no different in purport from the chapters of Oaths and Charges? You examination candidates have taken the imperial instructions to heart for years now and must surely know them thoroughly. Explain them to me.

Question: Since antiquity, those who have ruled All under Heaven have invariably regarded the imperial succession as a matter of great importance. We reverently received the enlightened edict establishing the crown prince. This is indeed sufficient to secure the foundation of the state, settle distinctions of status, and put the people’s minds at ease. Yet Jia Yi once said: “The fate of All under Heaven is bound to the crown prince. The goodness of the crown prince depends upon instructing him early and selecting his attendants. If his instruction is appropriate and his attendants upright, then the crown prince will be upright and All under Heaven will be settled.” This is a truly sound judgment. Thus, when Tai Jia was still very young, his tutor…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
保得伊尹而為令主成王居襁褓之日
太傅得周公而為賢君茲者列職
東宮罔匪正人易所謂蒙以養正書所謂罔
不在厥初生者
聖天子固已處之盡道矣而區區小臣願望之
誠猶自不能忘情也漢以下東宮之官
雖不在幼冲襁褓之年而隨時左右者
代有其人姑舉一二言之如恭謹無比
皆推可傅者必有所取如朝野咨詢為
===
世儒宗者必有所徵賜步輿而引入問
政者不知其何裨於治道得遺表而書
笏求諫者不知其何感於君心歡會賦
詩迹若放矣胡為而服其度量如肆飲
酒檢若疎矣胡為而稱其忠實之數子
者不知在
今日亦有所取顧當置之勿論而必欲上法
乎伊周也諸士子沐浴
聖澤作興有年指日皆當為
punctuated: 保得伊尹而為令主，成王居襁褓之日，太傅得周公而為賢君。茲者列職東宮，罔匪正人。《易》所謂「蒙以養正」，《書》所謂「罔不在厥初生」者，聖天子固已處之盡道矣。而區區小臣願望之誠，猶自不能忘情也。漢以下，東宮之官，雖不在幼冲襁褓之年，而隨時左右者，代有其人。姑舉一二言之：如恭謹無比，皆推可傅者，必有所取；如朝野咨詢，為世儒宗者，必有所徵。賜步輿而引入問政者，不知其何裨於治道？得遺表而書笏求諫者，不知其何感於君心？歡會賦詩，迹若放矣，胡為而服其度量？如肆飲酒，檢若疎矣，胡為而稱其忠實？之數子者，不知在今日亦有所取，顧當置之勿論，而必欲上法乎伊周也？諸士子沐浴聖澤，作興有年，指日皆當為
translation_en:
…having Yi Yin as his guardian, he became an excellent ruler. When King Cheng was still in swaddling clothes, he had the Duke of Zhou as Grand Preceptor and became a worthy sovereign. Now all those appointed to offices in the Eastern Palace are upright men. As for what the Book of Changes calls “nurturing rectitude in the inexperienced,” and what the Book of Documents calls “everything depends upon the beginning of life,” the sagely Son of Heaven has indeed made arrangements fully in accordance with the Way. Yet this humble minor servant, in the sincerity of his hopes, still cannot put his concern aside.

From the Han onward, even when the heir apparent was no longer an infant or in swaddling clothes, every age had men who served as Eastern Palace officials, attending him as circumstances required. Let us cite just one or two examples. A man whose reverence and circumspection were beyond compare, whom everyone recommended as fit to be a tutor, must have had qualities worth choosing. A man consulted by court and country alike, who was a leading Confucian scholar of his age, must have had merits to substantiate his reputation. Of the man granted a sedan chair and ushered in to be consulted on government, what contribution did he make to the art of governing? In the case of the man whose final memorial prompted the ruler to write on his court tablet and seek remonstrance, what was it that moved the ruler’s heart? One man composed poems at convivial gatherings, his conduct seemingly unrestrained: why was his magnanimity nevertheless admired? Another apparently drank freely [?], his self-discipline seemingly lax: why was he nevertheless praised for loyalty and sincerity? Might these several men also offer something worth adopting today? Or should we set them aside without discussion and insist on reaching back to take Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou as our models?

You candidates have bathed in the imperial beneficence and have been encouraged and cultivated for years. Before long, you should all serve as …

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國家任使其必有忠愛保護之誠可爲
明天子獻者請言之毋隱
問布衣而先廊廟之憂匹夫而繫古今之
慮故曰高山仰止景行行止又曰他山
之石可以攻玉人之賢否得失皆不可
不知而亦不可無定論也試與諸士子
言之天命有德也何以有嗔而與人官
者有笑而不與人官者天討有罪也何
以有專尚仁恕者有一於慘刻者同一
===
事人也有全君者有爲母者孰爲是歟
同一交友也有順友者有賣友者孰爲
失歟任人而逸與夫任己而勞有優劣
歟减竈示弱與夫增竈示強有智否歟
功名損於治郡果其才之有局耶北伐
竟無成功果其名之不副耶壞相白麻
卒以諫顯似可取也而君子又作爭臣
論以譏之其論然耶否耶瘞鹿於圃不
受饋遺似可羡也而或者又以爲矯激
punctuated:
國家任使，其必有忠愛保護之誠可爲明天子獻者，請言之毋隱。
問：布衣而先廊廟之憂，匹夫而繫古今之慮。故曰：「高山仰止，景行行止。」又曰：「他山之石，可以攻玉。」人之賢否得失，皆不可不知，而亦不可無定論也。試與諸士子言之。天命有德也，何以有嗔而與人官者，有笑而不與人官者？天討有罪也，何以有專尚仁恕者，有一於慘刻者？同一事人也，有全君者，有爲母者，孰爲是歟？同一交友也，有順友者，有賣友者，孰爲失歟？任人而逸，與夫任己而勞，有優劣歟？减竈示弱，與夫增竈示強，有智否歟？功名損於治郡，果其才之有局耶？北伐竟無成功，果其名之不副耶？壞相白麻，卒以諫顯，似可取也，而君子又作《爭臣論》以譏之，其論然耶否耶？瘞鹿於圃，不受饋遺，似可羡也，而或者又以爲矯激
translation_en:
…to serve the state. Surely you have sincere thoughts of loyalty, devotion, and protection to offer the enlightened Son of Heaven. Please state them without reserve.
Question: Even as a commoner, one anticipates the concerns of the court; even as a private individual, one takes to heart the concerns of past and present. Thus it is said, “We look up to the lofty mountain; we follow the great road.” It is also said, “Stones from other mountains can be used to polish jade.” One must understand people's worthiness or unworthiness, their successes and failings, and must also reach settled judgments about them. Let us discuss these matters with you candidates. Heaven charges the virtuous with office: why, then, have some bestowed office on a person while angry, whereas others have smiled yet withheld office? Heaven punishes the guilty: why have some exclusively prized benevolence and forbearance, while others have devoted themselves entirely to cruelty and severity? In serving another, some have preserved their lord, while others have acted for their mother: which was right? In friendship, some have accommodated their friends, while others have betrayed them: which was at fault? Is entrusting tasks to others and enjoying ease superior or inferior to taking tasks upon oneself and toiling? In reducing cooking fires to display weakness or increasing them to display strength, was one wise and the other unwise? When a man's achievements and reputation suffered through his administration of a commandery, was it truly because his abilities were limited? When a northern expedition ultimately achieved no success, was it truly because the man's abilities did not match his reputation? Destroying the white-hemp edict appointing a chief councillor [?] and ultimately becoming renowned for remonstrance would seem commendable; yet a gentleman wrote the Discourse on Remonstrating Officials to criticize him. Was that judgment correct or not? Burying a deer in a garden and refusing gifts would seem admirable; yet some considered this affected and extreme…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而議之其說是耶非耶諸士子抱藝而
來其於人物賢否得失評論之乆矣請
陳所見以驗格物窮理之學
問莫為之先後將何述莫為之後先將何
傳故生乎先者冀後人以繼述而生乎
後者景先哲以依歸且湖廣巨藩人物
無代無之諸士子生長於斯其於鄉先
達豈無知之審而可以諭人者乎濂溪
周子生於舂陵也其道何傳二程夫子
===
生於黃陂也其實何據胡文定嘗與張
南軒講道於衡山矣所得者何學張宣
公嘗與朱晦庵講道於湘潭矣所窮者
何理諸葛亮之起隆中其出師二表詞
氣何所比元次山之居道州其中興一
頌得失何所議屈原之事楚懷王忠矣
而其離騷之賦胡為乎怨伯奇之事尹
吉甫孝矣而其履霜之操胡為乎悲諸
士子其詳言之以觀所以景行先哲者
punctuated:
而議之，其說是耶非耶？諸士子抱藝而來，其於人物賢否得失評論之乆矣。請陳所見，以驗格物窮理之學。
問：莫為之先，後將何述？莫為之後，先將何傳？故生乎先者冀後人以繼述，而生乎後者景先哲以依歸。且湖廣巨藩，人物無代無之。諸士子生長於斯，其於鄉先達，豈無知之審而可以諭人者乎？濂溪周子生於舂陵也，其道何傳？二程夫子生於黃陂也，其實何據？胡文定嘗與張南軒講道於衡山矣，所得者何學？張宣公嘗與朱晦庵講道於湘潭矣，所窮者何理？諸葛亮之起隆中，其出師二表詞氣何所比？元次山之居道州，其中興一頌得失何所議？屈原之事楚懷王忠矣，而其離騷之賦胡為乎怨？伯奇之事尹吉甫孝矣，而其履霜之操胡為乎悲？諸士子其詳言之，以觀所以景行先哲者
translation_en:
…and criticized him: is this view right or wrong? You candidates have come bearing your scholarly accomplishments and have long assessed the worthiness and unworthiness, successes and failings of historical figures. Please set forth your views, so that your learning in investigating things and fathoming principles may be tested.
Policy question: If none came before, what would those coming after carry forward? If none came after, what would those coming before transmit? Thus, those born earlier hope that later generations will continue their work, while those born later look up to earlier worthies as their guides. Huguang is a great province, and no generation has lacked outstanding figures. You candidates were born and raised here: surely there are distinguished predecessors of your native region whom you know thoroughly enough to explain to others?
Master Zhou Lianxi was born in Chongling: what was the transmission of his Way? The two Masters Cheng were born in Huangpi: what evidence establishes this fact? Hu Wending once discussed the Way with Zhang Nanxuan at Hengshan [?]: what learning did they acquire? Lord Zhang Xuan once discussed the Way with Zhu Hui'an at Xiangtan: what principles did they fathom? Zhuge Liang emerged from Longzhong: to what may the language and spirit of his two Memorials on Dispatching the Army be compared? Yuan Cishan resided in Daozhou: what merits and faults have been debated in his Ode to the Restoration? Qu Yuan served King Huai of Chu loyally, yet why does his rhapsody Encountering Sorrow express resentment? Boqi served Yin Jifu with filial devotion, yet why does his zither song Treading on Frost express grief? You candidates should discuss these matters fully, so that we may see how you take the earlier worthies as models…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
何如
問古人謂識時務者在俊傑故問馬於伯
樂而良馬可知問材於公輸而良材可
得理必然也且天下之事可言者多矣
姑舉其切於湖藩者與諸士子商之災
荒在所恤也湖民往歲乾旱今年水溢
疲則甚矣何以救之風俗在所正也湖
民尚鬼好遊勁悍獷夷習則敝矣何以
革之原渚異居農賈無定流移可畏也
===
安得如古之居民按堵乎旅行野處恒
遭剽竊賊盜可憂也安得如古之路不
拾遺乎武昌漢陽適當都會之衝而行
伍多缺未免有防禦不及之憂古者兵
農之制可復耶德安安陸方有營繕之
舉而工費甚繁未免有會計不足之慮
古者榷筭之策可用耶刁頑相訐而獄
訟蝟興清之何術蠻酋相混而豪強狼
拒抑之何方諸士子積學待問行當有
punctuated:
何如？

問：古人謂識時務者在俊傑，故問馬於伯樂而良馬可知，問材於公輸而良材可得，理必然也。且天下之事可言者多矣，姑舉其切於湖藩者，與諸士子商之。災荒在所恤也，湖民往歲乾旱，今年水溢，疲則甚矣，何以救之？風俗在所正也，湖民尚鬼好遊，勁悍獷夷，習則敝矣，何以革之？原渚異居，農賈無定，流移可畏也，安得如古之居民按堵乎？旅行野處，恒遭剽竊，賊盜可憂也，安得如古之路不拾遺乎？武昌、漢陽適當都會之衝，而行伍多缺，未免有防禦不及之憂，古者兵農之制可復耶？德安、安陸方有營繕之舉，而工費甚繁，未免有會計不足之慮，古者榷筭之策可用耶？刁頑相訐，而獄訟蝟興，清之何術？蠻酋相混，而豪強狼拒，抑之何方？諸士子積學待問，行當有
translation_en:
…what this amounts to?

Question: The ancients said that outstanding men are those who understand the needs of the times. Thus, by asking Bo Le about horses, one can recognize fine horses; by asking Gongshu about timber, one can obtain fine timber. This necessarily follows from the nature of things. There are many affairs in the realm that merit discussion. Let us select those of immediate concern to Huguang Province and discuss them with you candidates.

Disaster and famine call for relief. The people of Huguang suffered drought in past years and flooding this year; they are utterly exhausted. How can they be succored? Customs call for correction. The people of Huguang venerate spirits and delight in idle wandering; they are fierce, violent, and uncivilized. Their habits have become corrupt. How can these be reformed? They dwell variously on plains and river islets, with no settled commitment to farming or trade. Their wandering and displacement are alarming. How can we achieve the security of ancient times, when people lived peacefully in their homes? Those traveling the roads or lodging in the open constantly suffer robbery and theft. Brigandage is a cause for concern. How can we achieve the conditions of ancient times, when no one pocketed things lost on the road?

Wuchang and Hanyang stand at major metropolitan crossroads, yet their military ranks have many vacancies. There is inevitably concern that their defenses may prove inadequate. Can the ancient system uniting soldiering and farming be restored? Construction and repair projects are now underway in De’an and Anlu, and expenditure on the work is enormous. There is inevitably concern that the available funds may be insufficient. Can ancient policies of monopoly revenues and taxation be employed?

The crafty and recalcitrant bring accusations against one another, and lawsuits spring up like a hedgehog’s bristles. By what means can these be cleared away? Tribal chieftains intermingle [?], while powerful local men resist like wolves. By what means can they be restrained? You candidates have accumulated learning in readiness for questioning and will soon have…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
民社之責願著于篇以觀經濟毋托之
曰君子思不出其位
punctuated: 民社之責，願著于篇，以觀經濟，毋托之曰：「君子思不出其位。」
translation_en: …responsibility for the people and the altars of the soil. Please set forth your views in writing, so that your ability in statecraft may be assessed. Do not take refuge in the saying: “The gentleman’s thoughts do not go beyond his station.”

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人八十五名
第一名楊褫常德府學生書
第二名何孟春郴州學生易

Comment by Examiner Liang, Instructor: Pure and correct; worthy of selection.

Neither obscure what one already understands nor force a claim to understand what one has yet to grasp: this is how the sage instructs the worthy. How imperative it is that learners not deceive themselves! What they already understand they certainly must not obscure; but can they force what they do not understand into a claim of understanding? Formerly, Zilu insisted on treating what he did not know as knowledge. Thus the Master instructed him, as if saying: “The affairs and principles of the world are inexhaustible, while what my mind knows is limited. The essential way to knowledge lies simply in not deceiving oneself. Thus, concerning the principles inherent in affairs, if one can truly know how things ought to be, distinguishing clearly without any doubt, and can plainly perceive why they are so, understanding fully without any perplexity, even illumination by a lamp or reckoning by counting could not surpass this clarity. When one knows in this manner, one says: ‘In this matter, I see the end from its beginning and know the interior from its exterior. Seeking within myself, I reflect …

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
昭昭之可信驗之於外非復昏昏之可倫是吾
所已知者也此知之者實以為知而勿自欺以
為不知焉若或理之寓於事者未能真知其當
然而猶涉於想像未能灼見其所以然而猶滯
於恍惚欲條分縷析焉不可得也不知如此則
曰我於此得其似而未見其真知其一而未達
其二影響之間冥然罔覺之尚在議擬之際豁
然貫通之未能是吾所不知者也此不知者實
以為不知而勿自欺以為知焉夫然則心無自
===
欺之蔽知有可盡之理汝由也其亦於斯乎致
力歟大抵子路好勇勇本美德也好勇而過則
喜於自高而不欲下人故強所不知以為知者
有焉噫此豈學者之心哉獨不觀未信之對漆
雕開特見說於夫子乎厥後子路以正名為迂
而卒不免於孔悝之難其未能深念夫子之教
也可惜哉
以王季為父以武王為子
謝訥
punctuated:
昭昭之可信，驗之於外，非復昏昏之可倫，是吾所已知者也。此知之者，實以為知，而勿自欺以為不知焉。若或理之寓於事者，未能真知其當然，而猶涉於想像；未能灼見其所以然，而猶滯於恍惚，欲條分縷析焉，不可得也。不知如此，則曰：「我於此，得其似而未見其真，知其一而未達其二，影響之間，冥然罔覺之尚在；議擬之際，豁然貫通之未能，是吾所不知者也。」此不知者，實以為不知，而勿自欺以為知焉。夫然，則心無自欺之蔽，知有可盡之理。汝由也，其亦於斯乎致力歟？大抵子路好勇，勇本美德也。好勇而過，則喜於自高而不欲下人，故強所不知以為知者有焉。噫！此豈學者之心哉？獨不觀未信之對，漆雕開特見說於夫子乎？厥後子路以正名為迂，而卒不免於孔悝之難，其未能深念夫子之教也，可惜哉！
以王季為父，以武王為子。
謝訥
translation_en:
…its clarity can be trusted; tested against external things, it is no longer comparable to dim confusion. This is what I already know. What one thus knows, one should truly acknowledge as known, without deceiving oneself into calling it unknown. If, however, one has not truly understood how the principles embodied in things ought to operate, and still resorts to conjecture, or has not clearly perceived why they are so, and remains caught in vague impressions, one cannot distinguish their strands and analyze them in detail. When one’s lack of knowledge is like this, one should say: “In this matter, I have grasped a semblance but have not seen the truth; I know one aspect but have not comprehended the other. Amid shadows and echoes, obscurity and unawareness remain; in deliberation and conjecture, I have yet to attain clear and comprehensive understanding. This is what I do not know.” What one thus does not know, one should truly acknowledge as unknown, without deceiving oneself into calling it known. Then the mind will be free of the obscuration of self-deception, and knowledge will have principles it can fully comprehend. You, You, should you not devote your efforts to this?
Generally speaking, Zilu was fond of courage, and courage is inherently a fine virtue. Yet when fondness for courage goes too far, one delights in exalting oneself and is unwilling to defer to others. Thus one may insist on treating what one does not know as known. Alas! Can this be the disposition of a learner? Consider Qidiao Kai’s reply that he was not yet confident: did it not win the Master’s particular approval? Later, Zilu regarded the rectification of names as impractical, and in the end failed to escape the calamity involving Kong Kui. How regrettable that he could not reflect deeply upon the Master’s teaching!
“Having Wang Ji as his father and King Wu as his son.”
Xie Ne.

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導沈批明白條暢可取
同考試官教諭強批詞順理明非穉筆所及
同考試官教諭吳批說出文王無憂之意殆無餘蘊
考試官教諭何批理明而詞贍可上𦘕
考試官教諭梁批簡而文此作近之
有賢王以為之先有聖王以為之後此聖人所
以無憂也盖父先乎我而子則後我者也文王
父賢而子聖則先後有其人矣夫何憂之有哉
中庸引孔子之言謂夫欲知文王之無憂當觀
===
文王之父子且人孰無父也父如瞽瞍焉如伯
鯀焉則上無所承矣惟我文王則以王季而為
父焉夫王季有周之賢王也克明克類有王此
大邦之德積功累仁有其勤王家之休王季之
賢如此而文王父之則父為賢父而先於我者
有其人矣人孰無子也子如丹朱焉如商均焉
則下無所授矣惟我文王則以武王而為子焉
夫武王有周之聖王也世德作求足以收三分
有二之天下永言孝思足以成九年未集之大
punctuated:
同考試官訓導沈批：明白條暢，可取。
同考試官教諭強批：詞順理明，非穉筆所及。
同考試官教諭吳批：說出文王無憂之意，殆無餘蘊。
考試官教諭何批：理明而詞贍，可上𦘕。
考試官教諭梁批：簡而文，此作近之。
有賢王以為之先，有聖王以為之後，此聖人所以無憂也。盖父先乎我，而子則後我者也。文王父賢而子聖，則先後有其人矣，夫何憂之有哉？《中庸》引孔子之言，謂夫欲知文王之無憂，當觀文王之父子。且人孰無父也？父如瞽瞍焉，如伯鯀焉，則上無所承矣。惟我文王，則以王季而為父焉。夫王季，有周之賢王也。克明克類，有王此大邦之德；積功累仁，有其勤王家之休。王季之賢如此，而文王父之，則父為賢父，而先於我者有其人矣。人孰無子也？子如丹朱焉，如商均焉，則下無所授矣。惟我文王，則以武王而為子焉。夫武王，有周之聖王也。世德作求，足以收三分有二之天下；永言孝思，足以成九年未集之大
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Shen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Clear, coherent, and fluent; worthy of selection.”
Associate Examiner Qiang, Instructor, comments: “The language flows smoothly and the reasoning is clear—beyond the reach of an immature writer.”
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “It explains why King Wen was free from sorrow, leaving virtually nothing unexpressed.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the language ample; it merits an upper grading mark [?].”
Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “Concise yet elegant: this composition approaches that ideal.”
With a worthy king preceding him and a sage king following him, this sage had no cause for sorrow. A father precedes me, while a son follows me. King Wen’s father was worthy and his son a sage: with the right men both before and after him, what cause could he have for sorrow? The Doctrine of the Mean quotes Confucius to say that, to understand King Wen’s freedom from sorrow, one should consider his father and son.
Who does not have a father? But if one’s father were like Gusou or Bo Gun, there would be nothing to inherit from the preceding generation. Our King Wen, however, had King Ji as his father. King Ji was a worthy king of Zhou. Discerning and able to distinguish good from evil, he possessed the virtue needed to rule this great state; accumulating achievements and benevolence, he won distinction through his diligent service to the royal house. Such was King Ji’s worthiness. With him as his father, King Wen had a worthy father: the man who preceded him was indeed the right one.
Who does not have a son? But if one’s son were like Danzhu or Shangjun, there would be no one to whom to transmit one’s legacy. Our King Wen, however, had King Wu as his son. King Wu was a sage king of Zhou. Continuing the virtue of his forebears and pursuing their aims, he was capable of bringing together the realm of which they had held two-thirds; ever mindful of filial duty, he was capable of completing the great … that had remained unaccomplished for nine years.

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
統武王之聖如此而文王子之則子為聖子而
後於我者有其人矣有賢父以為之先而上有
所承有聖子以為之後而下有所授文王俯仰
於其間夫復何憂哉是則父子重光祖孫一道
或以聖而繼賢或以聖而繼聖文王之事如此
宜中庸引之以明道之費也歟抑考周家王業
之成雖在於武王得天下之時而天命之定已
見於泰伯讓王季之日泰伯當立而不立文王
可為而不為故皆謂之至德然非文王之聖無
===
以垂武王之統非泰伯之讓無以成王季之功
遡而言之愚則曰武王以文王為父文王以王
季為父王季以泰伯為兄
禹之行水也行其所無事也
楊禠
同考試官訓導閔批詞不雕琢亦得大禹行水之智錄
為好奇者式
同考試官學正侯批詞簡而意備可羨
考試官教諭何批明暢
punctuated:
統。武王之聖如此，而文王子之，則子為聖子，而後於我者有其人矣。有賢父以為之先，而上有所承；有聖子以為之後，而下有所授。文王俯仰於其間，夫復何憂哉？是則父子重光，祖孫一道，或以聖而繼賢，或以聖而繼聖。文王之事如此，宜《中庸》引之以明道之費也歟！抑考周家王業之成，雖在於武王得天下之時，而天命之定，已見於泰伯讓王季之日。泰伯當立而不立，文王可為而不為，故皆謂之至德。然非文王之聖，無以垂武王之統；非泰伯之讓，無以成王季之功。遡而言之，愚則曰：武王以文王為父，文王以王季為父，王季以泰伯為兄。

禹之行水也，行其所無事也。
楊禠

同考試官訓導閔批：詞不雕琢，亦得大禹行水之智，錄為好奇者式。
同考試官學正侯批：詞簡而意備，可羨。
考試官教諭何批：明暢。
translation_en:
…dynastic succession. Such was the sageliness of King Wu, and King Wen had him as his son: his son was thus a sage, and there was a worthy person to follow him. With a worthy father preceding him, he had a legacy to inherit from above; with a sage son following him, he had someone below to whom he could transmit it. King Wen, looking upward and downward between them, had what further cause for concern? Thus father and son shone in succession, and grandfather and grandson followed the same Way: in one case a sage succeeded a worthy man, and in the other a sage succeeded a sage. Such were King Wen’s circumstances. Was it not fitting that the Doctrine of the Mean cited them to illuminate the far-reaching operation of the Way?

Moreover, although the royal enterprise of the house of Zhou reached fulfillment when King Wu gained All under Heaven, the settling of Heaven’s Mandate was already evident on the day Taibo yielded his place to Wang Ji. Taibo was entitled to succeed but did not; King Wen could have taken action but refrained. Hence both were said to possess consummate virtue. Yet without King Wen’s sageliness, there would have been no foundation for King Wu’s dynastic succession; without Taibo’s yielding, there would have been no means of bringing Wang Ji’s achievement to fruition. Tracing the matter backward, I would humbly say: King Wu had King Wen as his father; King Wen had Wang Ji as his father; and Wang Ji had Taibo as his elder brother.

“When Yu guided the waters, he guided them along courses requiring no interference.”
Yang Si 楊禠

Associate Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The wording is unembellished, and it also captures the wisdom with which the Great Yu guided the waters. Selected as a model for those who seek novelty.”

Associate Examiner Hou, School Instructor, comments: “The wording is concise, yet the meaning is complete. Admirable.”

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Clear and fluent.”

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭梁批典雅可觀
聖人有事於天下而以無事處事焉盖禹之治
水水之道也曽何以私智穿鑿而有所事哉孟
子論智而言此謂夫天下之理本皆利順小智
之人務為穿鑿獨不觀禹之行水乎當堯之時
洪水横流禹也為司空之官任平治之責疏三
江導九河除氾濫於滔天之日俾九州之一壑
者於是乎各有所歸而平成之休以臻焉决汝
漢排淮泗去壅塞於懐襄之際俾四海之一區
===
者於是乎各得其乂而府事之養以興焉禹於
此夫豈以私智為之哉盖循其源而濬其流因
其流而通其道築堤堙泉非所事也而處有事
於無事搏躍激行非所為也而運有為於無為
三江九河因其自然之勢而疏之導之爾初何
造作於其間汝漢淮泗順其自然之性而决之
排之爾初何矯揉於其内夫以禹之治水而行
所無事如此禹之智大矣使智者之處事亦若
是焉其尚何惡於智哉抑論之鯀與禹皆治水
punctuated:
考試官教諭梁批：典雅可觀。

聖人有事於天下，而以無事處事焉。盖禹之治水，水之道也，曽何以私智穿鑿而有所事哉？孟子論智而言此，謂夫天下之理，本皆利順，小智之人務為穿鑿，獨不觀禹之行水乎？當堯之時，洪水横流，禹也為司空之官，任平治之責，疏三江，導九河，除氾濫於滔天之日，俾九州之一壑者，於是乎各有所歸，而平成之休以臻焉；决汝漢，排淮泗，去壅塞於懐襄之際，俾四海之一區者，於是乎各得其乂，而府事之養以興焉。禹於此，夫豈以私智為之哉？盖循其源而濬其流，因其流而通其道。築堤堙泉，非所事也，而處有事於無事；搏躍激行，非所為也，而運有為於無為。三江九河，因其自然之勢而疏之導之爾，初何造作於其間？汝漢淮泗，順其自然之性而决之排之爾，初何矯揉於其内？夫以禹之治水，而行所無事如此，禹之智大矣！使智者之處事亦若是焉，其尚何惡於智哉？抑論之，鯀與禹皆治水
translation_en:
Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “Classical elegance, worthy of admiration.”

When a sage undertakes affairs in the world, he handles them without contrived intervention. Yu’s control of the waters followed the Way of water itself: how could he ever have imposed his own cleverness, forcing things into artificial arrangements? Mencius spoke of this when discussing wisdom. His meaning was that the inherent patterns of all things naturally permit smooth passage, yet men of petty cleverness devote themselves to contrivance. Have they alone failed to observe how Yu guided the waters?

In Yao’s time, floodwaters ran unchecked. Yu held the office of Minister of Works and bore responsibility for bringing them under control. He cleared the Three Rivers and guided the Nine Rivers, eliminating the inundation when the waters towered to the sky. Thus the waters that had made the Nine Regions a single abyss each found their proper outlet, and the blessings of a land made level and orderly were attained. He opened channels for the Ru and Han and drained the Huai and Si, removing obstructions when the floods engulfed hills and rose over heights. Thus the lands within the Four Seas, which had become one expanse of water, each attained order, and the means of sustaining life through the six storehouses and three affairs flourished.

In doing this, did Yu rely on his own cleverness? He followed the waters to their sources and dredged their courses; he worked with their flow and opened their channels. Building embankments and blocking springs were not his task: he managed affairs through an absence of contrived intervention. Making water leap upward by striking it or forcing it along was not his practice: he accomplished purposeful action through nonaction. With the Three Rivers and Nine Rivers, he merely followed their natural configuration in clearing and guiding them. What artificial manipulation did he ever introduce? With the Ru, Han, Huai, and Si, he merely followed their natural disposition in opening and draining them. What coercion did he ever apply?

Since Yu controlled the waters by proceeding without contrived intervention in this way, great indeed was his wisdom! If those who exercise wisdom likewise handled affairs in this manner, what grounds would there still be for disliking wisdom? To consider the matter further, Gun and Yu both controlled the waters …

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
者也鯀嘗以無功被殛禹則以大功受賞夫水
一也以鯀則不治以禹則治之何耶盖鯀之治
水以鯀治水禹之治水以水治水此所以功業
頓殊而成敗異勢也然則有志於大智者可不
以禹為法以鯀為戒乎
易
節以制度不傷財不害民
朱祺
同考試官訓導吳批此題作者類能析而為文理明詞
===
暢無踰此篇
考試官教諭何批明淨可嘉
考試官教諭梁批有節用愛人意非徒作者
聖人立當然之節故用有不匱而下無所損焉
甚矣人欲之無窮也向非聖人立當然之節欲
其用之不匱而下無所損其可得乎彖傳極言
節道如此謂夫天地非節無以成四時之功聖
人非節無以定萬用之限於是為之禮樂刑政
以品節乎天下為之法度紀綱以節制乎人心
punctuated:
者也。鯀嘗以無功被殛，禹則以大功受賞。夫水一也，以鯀則不治，以禹則治之，何耶？盖鯀之治水，以鯀治水；禹之治水，以水治水。此所以功業頓殊，而成敗異勢也。然則有志於大智者，可不以禹為法，以鯀為戒乎？

易
節以制度，不傷財，不害民。
朱祺

同考試官訓導吳批：此題作者類能析而為文，理明詞暢，無踰此篇。
考試官教諭何批：明淨可嘉。
考試官教諭梁批：有節用愛人意，非徒作者。

聖人立當然之節，故用有不匱，而下無所損焉。甚矣，人欲之無窮也！向非聖人立當然之節，欲其用之不匱，而下無所損，其可得乎？彖傳極言節道如此，謂夫天地非節，無以成四時之功；聖人非節，無以定萬用之限。於是為之禮樂刑政，以品節乎天下；為之法度紀綱，以節制乎人心。
translation_en:
…were both men who controlled the waters. Gun was put to death for failing to achieve results, whereas Yu was rewarded for his great accomplishments. The water was the same: under Gun it was not brought under control, but under Yu it was. Why? Because Gun, in controlling the waters, used his own will to govern them; Yu, in controlling the waters, used the nature of water itself to govern them. This is why their achievements differed so markedly, and why one failed while the other succeeded. Should those who aspire to great wisdom not take Yu as their model and Gun as their warning?

Book of Changes
“Regulating through institutions and measures, without injuring resources or harming the people.”
Zhu Qi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: Those writing on this topic generally know how to analyze it and compose an essay, but none surpasses this piece in clarity of reasoning and fluency of expression.
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: Clear and cleanly expressed; worthy of praise.
Comment by Examiner Liang, Instructor: It conveys the intent of being frugal in expenditure and caring for others; its author is more than a mere writer.

The sage establishes the proper restraints, so that resources for expenditure do not run short and those below suffer no loss. How boundless human desires are! Had the sage not established the proper restraints, could one hope to keep resources for expenditure from running short while ensuring that those below suffered no loss? The Commentary on the Judgments expounds the way of restraint to the fullest in these terms: without restraint, Heaven and Earth could not accomplish the work of the four seasons; without restraint, the sage could not set limits on the myriad expenditures. Accordingly, he establishes rites, music, punishments, and government to regulate all under Heaven in due degrees; he establishes laws, standards, guiding principles, and rules to restrain people’s hearts…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
如車服采章之有等截然名器之不紊也如宮
室器用之有辨凛然冠屨之不易也節以制度
如此殆見向焉費出無經未免侈用以傷財今
則眾志以定無復窮奢極欲之爲而公私之積
陳陳相因矣何有於傷財乎昔焉征斂無藝未
免傷財以害民今則國用以舒無復橫征暴斂
之政而遠近之民比比相安矣何有於害民乎
噫聖人盡節道之善如此此其所以爲天下人
物之宗主也歟彖傳極言之以示人其垂世立
===
教之意至矣由是觀之天地節而四時成者造
化自然之節也節以制度不傷財不害民者聖
人當然之節也造化節而成化育之功聖人節
而成致治之美此聖人所以有功於天地有功
於斯人也故曰如古之無聖人則人之類滅久
矣信夫
天之所助者順也人之所助者信也
何孟春

punctuated:
如車服采章之有等，截然名器之不紊也；如宮室器用之有辨，凛然冠屨之不易也。節以制度如此，殆見向焉費出無經，未免侈用以傷財；今則眾志以定，無復窮奢極欲之爲，而公私之積陳陳相因矣，何有於傷財乎？昔焉征斂無藝，未免傷財以害民；今則國用以舒，無復橫征暴斂之政，而遠近之民比比相安矣，何有於害民乎？噫！聖人盡節道之善如此，此其所以爲天下人物之宗主也歟！彖傳極言之以示人，其垂世立教之意至矣。由是觀之，天地節而四時成者，造化自然之節也；節以制度，不傷財、不害民者，聖人當然之節也。造化節而成化育之功，聖人節而成致治之美，此聖人所以有功於天地、有功於斯人也。故曰：「如古之無聖人，則人之類滅久矣。」信夫！

天之所助者順也，人之所助者信也。

translation_en:
…For example, gradations in carriages, robes, and ornamental insignia keep distinctions of rank and their emblems clearly ordered; distinctions in palaces, dwellings, utensils, and implements strictly prevent the interchange of caps and shoes—that is, the inversion of high and low. Such is regulation through institutions and rules. We may thus see that formerly expenditure lacked established standards, inevitably allowing extravagant consumption to deplete resources. Now, however, the aspirations of the multitude are settled; no longer do people indulge in boundless luxury and desire, and public and private stores accumulate, new stocks following old. How could resources be depleted? Formerly, taxation and exactions knew no bounds, inevitably depleting resources and harming the people. Now the state's financial needs are comfortably met; there are no more policies of arbitrary taxation and oppressive exaction, and people far and near live peaceably everywhere. How could the people be harmed?

Ah! The sage so fully realizes the goodness of the Way of restraint: is this not what makes him the sovereign guide of all people and things under Heaven? The Commentary on the Judgments expounds this fully to instruct people; its intent to establish teachings for succeeding ages is consummate. Viewed in this light, Heaven and Earth's restraint, through which the four seasons are accomplished, is the spontaneous restraint of the creative processes of nature. Regulation through institutions and rules, without depleting resources or harming the people, is the restraint that the sage ought to establish. Through restraint, nature accomplishes its work of transformation and nurture; through restraint, the sage achieves the excellence of good government. This is how the sage renders service to Heaven and Earth and to the people. Hence the saying: “Had there been no sages in antiquity, humankind would long since have perished.” How true!

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
暢故錄之
考試官教諭何批辭暢意足
考試官教諭梁批文義平正得天人所與之旨
天所與者由不違乎天之理人所與者由不違
乎人之理夫天人之理不外乎順信而已苟非
不違乎此理其何以得天人之與哉大傳釋大
有上九爻義如此且夫莫高匪天予奪莫測也
茲焉默而相之以祉元吉保佑命之受茲介福
是天助之者矣天之所助果安在耶其必履繩
===
蹈矩而身心不違乎天秉彝循理而舉措皆合
乎道靜與天契動與天游逆於理者未嘗萌諸
念慮義以制事禮以制心褻於天者未嘗形之
設施其順如此此天所以助之歟着夫莫衆匪
人從違靡定也茲焉不戒以孚皆於我乎盍簪
厥孚交如皆於我乎協力是人助之者矣人之
所助又安在耶其必有孚盈缶可以貫金石感
豚魚也有孚攣如可以應乎天化乎邦也慥慥
乎其誠慤而偽妄之不生恂恂乎其信實而欺

暢，故錄之。

Those whom Heaven supports do not contravene Heaven’s principles; those whom people support do not contravene human principles. Now, nothing is higher than Heaven, whose bestowals and withdrawals are unfathomable. On what, then, does Heaven’s assistance actually depend? Surely he must tread by the marking line and carpenter’s square, so that neither body nor mind contravenes Heaven; he must uphold the constant moral norms and follow principle, so that every action accords with the Way. In stillness he accords with Heaven; in movement he roams with Heaven. Nothing contrary to principle ever arises in his thoughts. He regulates affairs through righteousness and regulates his mind through ritual propriety. Nothing disrespectful toward Heaven ever takes form in his actions. Such is his compliance: is this not why Heaven assists him?
Now [?], none are more numerous than human beings, whose adherence and opposition are inconstant. Yet here, without admonition, they show trust and all gather around him; their mutual trust binds them together, and all join their efforts with his. This is the assistance of other people. His sincerity must bind others closely to him, sufficient to respond to Heaven and transform the state. title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
詐之無有其信如此此人所以助之歟噫天人
所助不出於順信如此是則上九履信思順而
尚賢其得自天祐之吉無不利者有由然矣抑
又論之天人有感通之機人心有同然之理然
亦必盡其在己者而後可得其在天者故信順
交盡得天人之助者有之矣未有不信不順能
得乎天而獲乎人也然則今之君子亦當於信
順求之毋徒委諸天而望諸人
書
===
王曰旨哉說乃言惟服乃不良于言予罔
聞于行說拜稽首曰非知之艱行之惟艱
楊褫

賢君契乎臣而美其言之可行大臣敬乎君而
冀其言之必行夫進言在臣而力行則在君也
punctuated:
詐之無有。其信如此，此人所以助之歟！噫！天人所助，不出於順信如此。是則上九履信思順而尚賢，其得自天祐之吉、無不利者，有由然矣。抑又論之，天人有感通之機，人心有同然之理，然亦必盡其在己者，而後可得其在天者。故信順交盡，得天人之助者有之矣；未有不信不順，能得乎天而獲乎人也。然則今之君子，亦當於信順求之，毋徒委諸天而望諸人。

translation_en:
…and there is no deceit. Such is his trustworthiness: is this not why people help him? Ah! The help given by Heaven and people rests on nothing beyond such compliance and trustworthiness. Thus, in the topmost nine, he practices trustworthiness, considers compliance, and honors the worthy. There is indeed a reason why he obtains the good fortune of being blessed by Heaven, with nothing unfavorable.

To discuss this further: Heaven and humanity have the capacity to respond to and communicate with one another, and human hearts share principles they alike acknowledge. Yet one must first fulfill all that lies within oneself before obtaining what rests with Heaven. Thus there are those who, fully realizing both trustworthiness and compliance, obtain the help of Heaven and people. Never has anyone lacking trustworthiness and compliance been able to gain Heaven’s favor and people’s support. Therefore, gentlemen of today should likewise seek these through trustworthiness and compliance, rather than merely leave matters to Heaven and look to other people.

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賢君契大臣之言而美之大臣安得不以力行
之難責望之哉昔高宗因傅說陳憲天聰明之
事而深有味於說之所言謂夫憲天聰明之說
汝固陳於我矣然而或以修已或以用人詞指
不同也旨哉斯言誠可致之於躬行焉或以處
事或以宅心條目非一也美矣此言信可施之
於踐履焉使汝括囊自晦而不良于言則修已
用人之道我固面墻如也果將何所知而致之
躬行乎使汝含章不發而弗善于言則處事宅
===
心之道我固聾聵如也抑將何所聞而施之踐
履乎傅說於是拜手以致其恭稽首以盡其禮
以為憲天聰明之說我已陳於王矣然而若修
已若用人王固知之於敷奏之頃也知之於耳
夫何難之有哉若處事若宅心王固聞之於獻
納之際也聞之於耳又何難之有哉要惟允以
蹈之使所謂修已所謂用人者知不徒知而真

When a worthy ruler finds accord with his great minister’s words and praises them, how could the minister fail to hold him to the difficult task of putting them earnestly into practice? Formerly, when Fu Yue expounded the matter of taking Heaven’s perceptiveness and discernment as a model, Gaozong found profound savor in his words. What, then, could I have heard and carried out in practice?”

考試官教諭何批：句皆警策。
考試官教諭梁批：此作甚佳，宜録。

小國事大之禮，非其地，春秋寓一國之意；望國事上之禮，非其地，春秋示一統之意。此蕭叔朝公于外不言所，諸侯朝王于外特言所，聖人於君臣名分之際嚴矣。且夫以小事大，諸侯交鄰國之道也。必朝于國都、于廟，乃其地焉。今魯莊因結昏於齊，為于穀之遇；蕭叔以附庸邦君，為朝魯之舉。合嘉禮於草茨之間，將恭敬於斯須之頃，是朝非其地，與後日王所之朝非地一也。春秋於此不言公所者，聖人意謂諸侯以一國為主者也。魯雖人望，不過五等之侯爵，其國止
translation_en:
…“melons great and small” [?]: does this not describe it?

Spring and Autumn Annals
“The lord of Xiao paid court to the duke”—the twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang. “The duke paid court at the king’s location”—the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.
Wang Bao

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The topic has clear explanations in the commentaries, yet writers offer a welter of conjectures, without any settled view. This essay grasps the principles correctly and expresses them with particular elegance. Surely its manner of development is exceptional!
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: Every sentence is incisive.
Comment by Examiner Liang, Instructor: This composition is excellent and should be included in the record.

When a small state performs the rites of serving a great one in an improper place, the Spring and Autumn Annals conveys the idea of the limits of a single state. When a prominent state performs the rites of serving its superior in an improper place, the Spring and Autumn Annals reveals the idea of unified sovereignty. Thus, when the lord of Xiao paid court to the duke outside the duke’s state, the text does not say “at his location”; when a regional lord paid court to the king away from the royal capital, it expressly says “at the king’s location.” The Sage was strict indeed concerning the distinctions of title and station between ruler and subject.

For the small to serve the great is the proper way for regional lords to deal with neighboring states. An audience must take place in the state capital, in the ancestral temple, to be in its proper place. Now Duke Zhuang of Lu, in connection with arranging a marriage alliance with Qi, held the meeting at Gu. The lord of Xiao, as ruler of a dependent state, undertook to pay court to Lu. He performed these auspicious rites amid thatched shelters, conveying his reverence in a fleeting encounter. This audience took place in an improper location, just as did the later audience at the king’s location.

That the Spring and Autumn Annals does not here say “at the duke’s location” reflects the Sage’s understanding that a regional lord presides over only a single state. title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於千乗其地儉於百里東蒙之外皆鄰封也曲
阜之外皆友邦也于穀齊地也魯何與焉區區
一國安敢上擬於天子哉不言公所一國之規
模盖如此若夫用下敬上人臣事天子之禮也
必朝于京師于廟乃其地焉今襄王因晉文克
楚而下勞諸侯即鑾輿所在而脩禮既非時巡
方岳之覲亦非述職京師之典是朝亦非其地
與前日蕭叔之朝非地同也春秋於此特言王
所者聖人盖謂王者以天下為家者也周雖不
===
振猶為天下之共主號祭之名尚存車服之制
未改駐蹕於此歟此即其所也行幸於彼歟彼
即其所也踐土行宫也天子在焉赫赫宗周安
可下同於列國哉特言王所一統之氣象盖如
此吁脩禮同非其地書法獨異其文聖人於君
臣名分之際其嚴乎雖然周自東遷以来地不
大於曹滕民不衆於邾莒較之齊魯大邦逕庭
矣吾夫子脩春秋獨拳拳於尊周雖一字之間
不少假借有王者起正名統實其庶幾乎此作
punctuated: 於千乗，其地儉於百里，東蒙之外皆鄰封也，曲阜之外皆友邦也。于穀，齊地也，魯何與焉？區區一國，安敢上擬於天子哉？不言公所，一國之規模盖如此。若夫用下敬上，人臣事天子之禮也，必朝于京師、于廟，乃其地焉。今襄王因晉文克楚而下勞諸侯，即鑾輿所在而脩禮，既非時巡方岳之覲，亦非述職京師之典，是朝亦非其地，與前日蕭叔之朝非地同也。《春秋》於此特言王所者，聖人盖謂王者以天下為家者也。周雖不振，猶為天下之共主，號祭之名尚存，車服之制未改。駐蹕於此歟？此即其所也。行幸於彼歟？彼即其所也。踐土，行宫也，天子在焉。赫赫宗周，安可下同於列國哉？特言王所，一統之氣象盖如此。吁！脩禮同非其地，書法獨異其文，聖人於君臣名分之際，其嚴乎！雖然，周自東遷以来，地不大於曹滕，民不衆於邾莒，較之齊魯大邦，逕庭矣。吾夫子脩《春秋》，獨拳拳於尊周，雖一字之間，不少假借。有王者起，正名統實，其庶幾乎此作
translation_en:
…to a thousand chariots, and its territory is confined within a hundred li. Beyond Dongmeng lie neighboring domains; beyond Qufu lie other states. Gu is territory of Qi: what claim does Lu have there? How could a mere single state dare to liken itself to the Son of Heaven above? The omission of “the duke’s location” reflects the limited compass of a single state.

As for honoring a superior from an inferior position, this is the ritual by which a subject serves the Son of Heaven. An audience must take place in the capital, in the ancestral temple, to be held in its proper setting. Now King Xiang, because Duke Wen of Jin had defeated Chu, came down to reward the regional lords, and the rites were performed wherever the royal carriage happened to be. This was neither an audience at the sacred mountains during a seasonal royal tour nor the ceremony of reporting on one’s duties in the capital. This audience, too, was held in an improper place, just like Xiao Shu’s earlier audience. The reason the Spring and Autumn Annals here expressly says “the king’s location” is that the Sage regarded the king as having all under Heaven for his home. Though Zhou had declined, its king remained the common sovereign of all under Heaven. Its sacrificial designation still survived [?], and its regulations for carriages and ceremonial dress had not changed. Did the royal carriage halt here? Then here was his proper place. Did he travel there? Then there was his proper place. Jiantu was a traveling palace: the Son of Heaven was there. How could the illustrious royal house of Zhou be brought down to the same level as the various states? The express use of “the king’s location” thus conveys the majesty of unified sovereignty.

Ah! In both cases the rites were performed in an improper place, yet the wording used to record them differs. How strict the Sage was concerning the distinctions of status between ruler and subject! Nevertheless, since Zhou’s eastward relocation, its territory had been no larger than Cao or Teng, and its population no greater than Zhu or Ju. It fell far short of great states such as Qi and Lu. Yet when our Master compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was devoted above all to honoring Zhou, allowing not the slightest latitude even in a single character. Should a true king arise to rectify names and bring actual conditions into unity, might he not come close to this intent in composing…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
經之意也噫為王道計為世道計信非聖人莫
能脩之
宋公楚子陳侯蔡侯鄭伯許男曹伯會于
盂執宋公以伐宋楚人使宜申來獻
捷俱僖公二十一年
方琛
同考試官教諭鄭批此篇專以為魯諱立說而辭
氣雍容𠅘經之巨擘歟
考試官教諭何批得大傳意
===
考試官教諭梁批義正辭嚴
望國不申義以抑外夷之强春秋特婉詞以諱
望國之惡此魯僖失安攘之道觀春秋書法而
意自見矣且魯以周公伯禽之裔號儒書秉禮
之邦膺懲之家法在焉安攘之責任係焉子孫
可不世守之乎乃今宋襄圖伯與楚會盂楚成
既伏兵車執宋公於壇坫之上乘勢而伐其國
又使宜申獻宋捷於曲阜之邦假威而脅夫魯
其執宋也以襄公欲繼桓烈方脩盟會肆威而
punctuated:
經之意也。噫！為王道計，為世道計，信非聖人莫能脩之。
宋公、楚子、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會于盂，執宋公以伐宋。楚人使宜申來獻捷。俱僖公二十一年。
方琛。
同考試官教諭鄭批：此篇專以為魯諱立說，而辭氣雍容，𠅘經之巨擘歟！
考試官教諭何批：得大傳意。
考試官教諭梁批：義正辭嚴。
望國不申義以抑外夷之强，《春秋》特婉詞以諱望國之惡。此魯僖失安攘之道，觀《春秋》書法而意自見矣。且魯以周公、伯禽之裔，號儒書秉禮之邦，膺懲之家法在焉，安攘之責任係焉，子孫可不世守之乎？乃今宋襄圖伯，與楚會盂。楚成既伏兵車，執宋公於壇坫之上，乘勢而伐其國，又使宜申獻宋捷於曲阜之邦，假威而脅夫魯。其執宋也，以襄公欲繼桓烈，方脩盟會，肆威而
translation_en:
…was the intention behind composing the Classic. Ah! To devise measures for the Kingly Way and for the moral order of the world—truly, none but a sage could have compiled it.
“The Duke of Song, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao met at Yu. They seized the Duke of Song and attacked Song. The men of Chu sent Yishen to present the spoils of victory.” Both entries are from the twenty-first year of Duke Xi.
Fang Chen.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “This essay bases its argument entirely on the concealment of Lu’s faults, yet its language and tone are composed and dignified. Surely a master of interpreting the Classic [?]!”
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “It captures the meaning of the Great Commentary.”
Comment by Examiner Liang, Instructor: “Its principles are correct and its language stern.”
When a leading state failed to uphold righteousness and restrain the power of foreign peoples, the Spring and Autumn Annals deliberately used indirect language to conceal that state’s wrongdoing. Here Duke Xi of Lu failed to follow the way of securing peace within and repelling threats from without; examination of the Annals’ manner of recording events makes its meaning plain. Moreover, Lu, ruled by descendants of the Duke of Zhou and Boqin, was reputed to be a state of Confucian learning [?] that upheld ritual. Its inherited precepts prescribed punitive action against aggressors, and responsibility for securing peace within and repelling threats from without rested upon it. Could its descendants fail to preserve these precepts generation after generation?
Yet now Duke Xiang of Song sought the hegemony and met with Chu at Yu. King Cheng of Chu concealed war chariots in ambush, seized the Duke of Song upon the ceremonial platform, and exploited his advantage to attack Song. He then sent Yishen to present the spoils of victory over Song to the state whose capital was Qufu, using this display of might to intimidate Lu. title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
陵轢之其獻捷也以諸侯從楚伐宋魯獨不與
矜威而恐動之楚之横逆莫此爲甚爲魯僖者
因宋捷之來守膺懲之訓拒其使而不受則理
直氣壯足以卻之國門之外矣聲其罪而致討
則詞嚴義正足以震乎漢水之濱矣柰何計不
出此偷安是圖甘受宋捷之獻而外攘之謀落
落其無聞隱忍蠻荆之侮而内安之策寥寥其
未見魯之不競如此聖人脩經意謂宋爲先代
之後與我魯同等也今遭楚執伐我受其捷而
===
不辭其於尊中國之義何有哉楚爲蠻夷之雄
與我魯異類也今敢伐盟主我受其捷而不慙
其於攘夷狄之義安在哉故於宜申來獻而不
曰宋捷特爲魯諱之也諱之雖婉其詞而公之
罪自不可得而掩矣雖然僖爲魯之賢君不能
申大義以攘荆楚尊中國固可罪也宋襄欲繼
齊桓之烈而與楚盟會豈攘戎狄尊王室之義
乎且猶不知鑒其覆轍至于泓之戰獨愛重傷
與二毛竊效帝王之兵卒以取敗爲天下笑何
punctuated: 陵轢之。其獻捷也，以諸侯從楚伐宋，魯獨不與，矜威而恐動之。楚之横逆，莫此爲甚。爲魯僖者，因宋捷之來，守膺懲之訓，拒其使而不受，則理直氣壯，足以卻之國門之外矣；聲其罪而致討，則詞嚴義正，足以震乎漢水之濱矣。柰何計不出此，偷安是圖，甘受宋捷之獻，而外攘之謀落落其無聞；隱忍蠻荆之侮，而内安之策寥寥其未見。魯之不競如此，聖人脩經，意謂宋爲先代之後，與我魯同等也，今遭楚執伐，我受其捷而不辭，其於尊中國之義何有哉？楚爲蠻夷之雄，與我魯異類也，今敢伐盟主，我受其捷而不慙，其於攘夷狄之義安在哉？故於宜申來獻，而不曰宋捷，特爲魯諱之也。諱之雖婉其詞，而公之罪自不可得而掩矣。雖然，僖爲魯之賢君，不能申大義以攘荆楚、尊中國，固可罪也。宋襄欲繼齊桓之烈而與楚盟會，豈攘戎狄、尊王室之義乎？且猶不知鑒其覆轍，至于泓之戰，獨愛重傷與二毛，竊效帝王之兵，卒以取敗，爲天下笑。何
translation_en: …and trampled upon him. As for presenting the spoils of victory, because the other lords had followed Chu in attacking Song while Lu alone had not participated, Chu flaunted its might to intimidate Lu. Nothing could exceed Chu’s brutality and defiance. In Duke Xi of Lu’s position, when the spoils from Song arrived, had he upheld the ancestral injunction to chastise aggressors, rejected the envoy, and refused the offering, the strength and confidence of a just cause would have sufficed to turn him back outside the capital gates. Had he proclaimed Chu’s crimes and undertaken a punitive expedition, his stern words and righteous cause would have sufficed to strike fear along the banks of the Han River. Why, then, did he devise no such course, seeking only an easy peace? He willingly accepted the spoils from Song, yet nothing was heard of any plan to repel external threats. He silently endured the insults of the barbarians of Jing, yet no policy for securing peace within was to be seen. Such was Lu’s weakness. In compiling the Classic, the Sage meant that Song, as the descendant state of a former dynasty, stood on an equal footing with our Lu. Now that Chu had seized its ruler and attacked its territory, if we accepted the spoils without refusing them, what regard did we show for the duty to honor the Central States? Chu was the strongest of the barbarians, of a different kind from our Lu. Now that it dared attack the leader of the covenant, if we accepted its spoils without shame, where was our commitment to repelling the barbarians? Thus, in recording Yishen’s arrival to present an offering, the text does not say “spoils from Song”: this omission specifically conceals Lu’s disgrace. Although the concealment makes the wording tactful, the duke’s guilt cannot thereby be hidden. Nevertheless, Duke Xi was a worthy ruler of Lu, and he certainly deserves blame for failing to uphold the great principle of repelling Jing-Chu and honoring the Central States. But Duke Xiang of Song wished to continue the achievements of Duke Huan of Qi, yet met with Chu to conclude a covenant. How could that accord with the duty to repel the Rong and Di and honor the royal house? Moreover, he still failed to learn from his earlier disaster. At the Battle of Hong, he cared only about sparing those already wounded and those with graying hair, presumptuously imitating the warfare of the ancient emperors and kings. In the end, he brought defeat upon himself and became the laughingstock of all under Heaven. How…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其迂疎之甚耶何以主盟當世耶先儒謂襄公
非特無功而又階亂詎不然
禮記
大司徒大司馬大司空以百官之成質于
天子
陳襄
同考試官教諭陳批講百官之成有考據必熟於經學者
同考試官教諭吳批題本艱於措詞而此篇安行於衆人
窘歩之餘當是作者
===
考試官教諭何批鋪叙詳整可嘉
考試官教諭梁批發揮百官質成處無餘蘊
大臣以所達羣臣之功而爲之考正於大君焉
蓋歲終獻功王者之盛典也大臣以百官位卑
而爲之考成於天子其尊君之意何如哉記王
制者謂夫一歲之成不進於上則情不通不考
於上則拳不立彼司會既先質矣大樂正大司
冦市又從質矣百官之質于三官者大司徒大
司馬大司空不爲之達於天子可乎是故次于
punctuated:
其迂疎之甚耶！何以主盟當世耶？先儒謂襄公非特無功，而又階亂，詎不然？

禮記

大司徒、大司馬、大司空以百官之成質于天子。

陳襄

同考試官教諭陳批：講百官之成，有考據，必熟於經學者。
同考試官教諭吳批：題本艱於措詞，而此篇安行於衆人窘歩之餘，當是作者。
考試官教諭何批：鋪叙詳整，可嘉。
考試官教諭梁批：發揮百官質成處，無餘蘊。

大臣以所達羣臣之功，而爲之考正於大君焉。蓋歲終獻功，王者之盛典也。大臣以百官位卑，而爲之考成於天子，其尊君之意何如哉！記王制者謂夫一歲之成，不進於上則情不通，不考於上則拳不立。彼司會既先質矣，大樂正、大司冦市又從質矣。百官之質于三官者，大司徒、大司馬、大司空不爲之達於天子，可乎？是故次于
translation_en:
…how extraordinarily impractical he was! How could he preside over the covenants of his age? Earlier Confucian scholars said that Duke Xiang not only achieved nothing but also paved the way for disorder. Was this not indeed so?

Book of Rites

“The Minister of Education, the Minister of War, and the Minister of Works submit the completed work of the hundred officials to the Son of Heaven for scrutiny.”

Chen Xiang

Associate Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is difficult to put into words, yet this essay proceeds with ease where others can scarcely find their footing. Its author surely deserves to be called an accomplished writer.”
Examiner He, an Instructor, comments: “The exposition is detailed and orderly: commendable.”
Examiner Liang, an Instructor, comments: “His elucidation of the submission of the hundred officials’ completed work for scrutiny leaves nothing unexplored.”

The great ministers take the accomplishments of the assembled officials that they transmit upward and have them examined and assessed before the sovereign. Presenting accomplishments at the year’s end is a grand institution of kingly government. Because the hundred officials hold low rank, the great ministers have their completed work assessed before the Son of Heaven. How profound is their intention to honor their ruler!

The author of the ‘Royal Regulations’ says that if a year’s accomplishments are not presented to the ruler, actual circumstances cannot be communicated; if they are not examined by the ruler, authority [?] cannot be established. As for the reports that the hundred officials submit to the three ministers, would it be acceptable for the Minister of Education, the Minister of War, and the Minister of Works not to transmit them to the Son of Heaven? Thus, next in rank below…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
冢宰掌邦敎敷五典者大司徒也次于司徒掌
邦政統六師者非大司馬乎又次于司馬掌邦
土居四民者非大司空乎當質成之日若大胥
若小胥之屬官不一也而一歲之費用有常經
若小司寇小司馬之屬職不同也而一歲之制
用有定數至若廛人質人廬人之類亦皆各有
所掌而各有一歲經用之制焉然以位卑不敢
專達故其屬於司徒司馬者皆書其計要而獻
之或當耶或否耶悉歸於一人掌握之中以聽
===
其平斷是雖司徒司馬何敢以上干乎其屬乎
司空者皆舉其計要而致之或宜耶或非耶咸
總於大君綱維之內以聽其平報是雖司空何
敢以上預乎吁先王崇重天功天職之意一何
至哉抑考周官司會之職以歲會考歲成專言
在內之王臣也虞書三載考績三考黜陟幽明
兼言在外之侯臣也王臣在內而近故考之不
欲疏侯臣在外而遠故考之不欲數因內外之
異爲疏數之期此先王之制歷萬世而無弊也
punctuated: 冢宰，掌邦敎、敷五典者，大司徒也。次于司徒，掌邦政、統六師者，非大司馬乎？又次于司馬，掌邦土、居四民者，非大司空乎？當質成之日，若大胥、若小胥之屬，官不一也，而一歲之費用有常經；若小司寇、小司馬之屬，職不同也，而一歲之制用有定數；至若廛人、質人、廬人之類，亦皆各有所掌，而各有一歲經用之制焉。然以位卑，不敢專達，故其屬於司徒、司馬者，皆書其計要而獻之。或當耶？或否耶？悉歸於一人掌握之中，以聽其平斷。是雖司徒、司馬，何敢以上干乎？其屬乎司空者，皆舉其計要而致之。或宜耶？或非耶？咸總於大君綱維之內，以聽其平報。是雖司空，何敢以上預乎？吁！先王崇重天功、天職之意，一何至哉！抑考《周官》司會之職，「以歲會考歲成」，專言在內之王臣也。《虞書》「三載考績，三考黜陟幽明」，兼言在外之侯臣也。王臣在內而近，故考之不欲疏；侯臣在外而遠，故考之不欲數。因內外之異，爲疏數之期，此先王之制，歷萬世而無弊也。
translation_en:
…the Grand Administrator: the official who administers the state's instruction and disseminates the five teachings is the Minister of Education. Next after the Minister of Education, is not the official who administers the state's government and commands the six armies the Minister of War? And next after the Minister of War, is not the official who administers the state's lands and settles the four classes of people the Minister of Works? When the time comes to submit accomplishments for scrutiny, officials such as the Senior and Junior Music Instructors hold different offices, yet their annual expenditures follow established rules. Officials such as the Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of War have different duties, yet their annual spending is governed by fixed amounts. As for the collectors of market dues, market inspectors, shaft makers, and the like, each likewise has particular responsibilities and prescribed rules for annual expenditure. Because their rank is low, however, they dare not report directly on their own authority. Thus those subordinate to the Ministers of Education and War all write out summaries of their accounts and present them. Are these proper or not? All are placed within the sovereign's grasp, awaiting his impartial judgment. Even the Ministers of Education and War—how could they dare encroach upon the authority above them? Those subordinate to the Minister of Works likewise submit summaries of their accounts. Are these appropriate or not? All are brought within the great ruler's governing authority, awaiting his impartial decision. Even the Minister of Works—how could he dare intervene in matters belonging to the authority above him? Ah! How profound was the intention of the former kings to honor the work and duties entrusted by Heaven!

Moreover, examining the duties of the Supervisor of Accounts in the Offices of Zhou, the statement that he “uses the annual accounts to assess the year's accomplishments” refers specifically to the king's ministers serving within the central government. The statement in the Documents of Yu that “performance was assessed every three years; after three assessments, the obscure and the illustrious were demoted or promoted” also encompasses the ministers of the regional lords serving outside it. The king's ministers served within and were nearby, so their assessments were not to be too infrequent. The regional lords' ministers served outside and were distant, so their assessments were not to be too frequent. The intervals between assessments were set according to this distinction between service within and outside the central government. Such was the system of the former kings: it could endure for ten thousand generations without giving rise to abuses.

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
此之謂大當然後聖人作爲父子君臣以
爲紀綱紀綱既正天下大定天下大定然
後正六律和五聲弦歌詩頌此之謂德音
德音之謂樂
李忠
同考試官教諭陳批本大註立說卓有定見
同考試官教諭吳批以大樂之作原於化洽禮序得旨
考試官教諭何批典雅純實此作近之
===
考試官教諭梁批講語以樂為重最是
聖王當大化之洽也必先序之以大禮而後和
之以大樂蓋王者治定功成而後制禮作樂也
化洽而禮序矣然後和之以樂則古樂豈易易
乎子夏告魏文侯問樂而推其原謂夫古昔盛
時天地順而四時當民有德而五穀昌疾疢不
作妖祥不生至和之薰蒸也大化之均調也大
當如此不有制作何以昭宣化育乎於是聖人
備禮樂之本操制作之柄以禮莫大於父子君
punctuated:
此之謂大當。然後聖人作爲父子君臣，以爲紀綱。紀綱既正，天下大定；天下大定，然後正六律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌。此之謂德音，德音之謂樂。
李忠
同考試官教諭陳批：本大註立說，卓有定見。
同考試官教諭吳批：以大樂之作原於化洽禮序，得旨。
考試官教諭何批：典雅純實，此作近之。
考試官教諭梁批：講語以樂為重，最是。
聖王當大化之洽也，必先序之以大禮，而後和之以大樂。蓋王者治定功成，而後制禮作樂也。化洽而禮序矣，然後和之以樂，則古樂豈易易乎？子夏告魏文侯問樂，而推其原，謂夫古昔盛時，天地順而四時當，民有德而五穀昌，疾疢不作，妖祥不生，至和之薰蒸也，大化之均調也。大當如此，不有制作，何以昭宣化育乎？於是聖人備禮樂之本，操制作之柄，以禮莫大於父子君
translation_en:
“This is called the great accord. Only then did the sage establish the relationships of father and son, ruler and minister, to serve as the guiding bonds. Once these bonds were set right, all under Heaven became firmly settled. Once all under Heaven was firmly settled, he then regulated the six pitch standards, harmonized the five notes, and sang the poems and hymns to stringed accompaniment. These are called the sounds of virtue; the sounds of virtue are what is meant by music.”
Li Zhong

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
臣也則作爲父子君臣之禮以爲六紀三綱之
目使諸父有善諸舅有義族人有叙昆弟有親
師長有尊朋友有舊焉使君爲臣綱父爲子綱
夫爲妻綱焉內外相維而倫理以明孰敢有不
正也小大相安而恩義以篤孰敢有不定也天
下大定而禮序矣樂於是乎作焉彼樂莫大乎
六律五聲也于以正夫黃鍾太簇姑洗蕤賓夷
則無射之六律而相生也有次和夫宮商角徵
羽之五聲而相宣也有節弦之琴瑟非溺音可
===
比歌之詩頌皆倫理所寓不謂德音而何由是
父子聽而和親君臣聽而和敬足以修身及家
平均天下非新樂可及矣謂之古樂不亦大哉
吁化洽禮序而樂之作也有關於治道如此大
抵樂記一篇論樂必先於禮論禮樂必先於天
地何哉盖聖王之制禮樂未有不本於造化者
子夏以此告魏文侯意有在耳惜乎文侯方不
知倦於聽鄭衛之音而唯恐卧於聽古樂又安
足以語此
punctuated:
臣也，則作爲父子君臣之禮，以爲六紀三綱之目，使諸父有善，諸舅有義，族人有叙，昆弟有親，師長有尊，朋友有舊焉；使君爲臣綱，父爲子綱，夫爲妻綱焉。內外相維而倫理以明，孰敢有不正也？小大相安而恩義以篤，孰敢有不定也？天下大定而禮序矣，樂於是乎作焉。彼樂莫大乎六律五聲也，于以正夫黃鍾、太簇、姑洗、蕤賓、夷則、無射之六律，而相生也有次；和夫宮、商、角、徵、羽之五聲，而相宣也有節。弦之琴瑟，非溺音可比；歌之詩頌，皆倫理所寓，不謂德音而何？由是父子聽而和親，君臣聽而和敬，足以修身及家，平均天下，非新樂可及矣。謂之古樂，不亦大哉！
吁！化洽禮序，而樂之作也有關於治道如此。大抵《樂記》一篇，論樂必先於禮，論禮樂必先於天地，何哉？盖聖王之制禮樂，未有不本於造化者。子夏以此告魏文侯，意有在耳。惜乎文侯方不知倦於聽鄭衛之音，而唯恐卧於聽古樂，又安足以語此？
translation_en:
…and ministers. Thus they established rites for fathers and sons, rulers and ministers, as the specific provisions of the Six Bonds and Three Guiding Relationships. These ensured kindness among paternal uncles, righteousness among maternal uncles, proper order among clan members, affection among brothers, respect for teachers and elders, and enduring ties among friends. They made the ruler the guiding principle for his ministers, the father for his sons, and the husband for his wife. With inner and outer relationships sustaining one another and ethical relations thereby clarified, who would dare fail to be upright? With great and small at peace with one another and affection and duty thereby strengthened, who would dare remain unsettled? Once all under Heaven was firmly settled and ritual order established, music was then created.
Nothing in music is more fundamental than the six pitch standards and five tones. Accordingly, they rectified the six pitch standards—Huangzhong, Taicu, Guxian, Ruibin, Yize, and Wuyi—so that their generation of one another followed a proper sequence. They harmonized the five tones—gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu—so that their mutual expression followed due measure. Played on the strings of the qin and se zithers, this music could not be compared with depraved sounds; sung in poems and hymns, it embodied ethical relationships throughout. What could it be called but the sound of virtue? Thus, when fathers and sons heard it, they became harmonious and affectionate; when rulers and ministers heard it, they became harmonious and respectful. It sufficed to cultivate oneself, extend that cultivation to the family, and bring equitable order to all under Heaven. Modern music could not equal it. Called ancient music, was it not indeed great!
Ah! When moral transformation had become pervasive and ritual order was established, the creation of music bore this close a relation to the way of governing. In general, the Record of Music always begins with ritual when discussing music, and with Heaven and Earth when discussing ritual and music. Why is this? Because the sage kings’ establishment of ritual and music invariably took its foundation from the creative transformations of the cosmos. Zixia had a particular purpose in telling this to Marquis Wen of Wei. Alas, Marquis Wen never tired of listening to the sounds of Zheng and Wei, yet feared only that he would fall asleep when listening to ancient music. How could he have been fit to discuss this?

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:

天位曰大寶何貴如之天下曰大器何重
如之天子曰大君何尊如之苟不大有所
作為奚足以稱此大寶堪此大器而當此
大任也耶揚雄曰天下為大治之在道不
亦小乎是則大有為者固不過擴充此道
而小天下於吾方寸間耳何則禮其皇極
之門禮必齋莊中正而後已義其共由之
路義必發强剛毅而後已不煦煦為仁而

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
文章必斡乾轉坤而後為大必經天緯地
而後為大必泰華不為高滄溟不為深而
後為大必萬彙不為繁八極不為廣而後
為大君將大有為若此任力而力易疲用
謀而謀有限如之何則可辟之良農有志
於大穫必得善稼者為之傭辟之良將有
志於大勝必擇善兵者為之掾大有為之
君欲大有為於天下而非用道德之大賢
吾見其倡之無與為和也行之無與為徒
===
也其農之不傭將之不掾而不餒且敗焉
者幾希夫君雖貴於用賢而賢非可以輕
致丹山之鳳不入於凡羅碧海之鯨不餌
於常釣麒麟不可以羈繫松柏不可以藩
籬道德之士抑豈可以召而臣之也哉故
大有為者或就而從學焉或師而後臣焉
不以崇高為尊而惟德是尊不以富貴為
樂而惟道是樂夫然後所謂大賢者變丘
林之志為廊廟之謀乾之同聲相應也泰
punctuated: 文章必斡乾轉坤而後為大，必經天緯地而後為大，必泰華不為高、滄溟不為深而後為大，必萬彙不為繁、八極不為廣而後為大。君將大有為若此，任力而力易疲，用謀而謀有限，如之何則可？辟之良農，有志於大穫，必得善稼者為之傭；辟之良將，有志於大勝，必擇善兵者為之掾。大有為之君欲大有為於天下，而非用道德之大賢，吾見其倡之無與為和也，行之無與為徒也。其農之不傭、將之不掾，而不餒且敗焉者，幾希！夫君雖貴於用賢，而賢非可以輕致。丹山之鳳不入於凡羅，碧海之鯨不餌於常釣，麒麟不可以羈繫，松柏不可以藩籬，道德之士抑豈可以召而臣之也哉？故大有為者，或就而從學焉，或師而後臣焉，不以崇高為尊而惟德是尊，不以富貴為樂而惟道是樂。夫然後所謂大賢者，變丘林之志為廊廟之謀，乾之同聲相應也，泰
translation_en:
…his cultural achievements can be called great only when they turn Heaven and Earth; only when they give order to Heaven and Earth as warp and weft; only when, beside them, Mount Tai and Mount Hua seem no longer high and the vast ocean no longer deep; only when the myriad things seem no longer numerous and the eight extremities of the world no longer extensive. If a ruler intends great accomplishments such as these, physical strength is easily exhausted when relied upon, and plans have their limits when employed. How, then, can he succeed? Consider a good farmer: if he aspires to a great harvest, he must obtain skilled cultivators to work for him. Consider a good general: if he aspires to a great victory, he must choose men skilled in warfare to serve as his aides. If a ruler bent on great accomplishments wishes to achieve great things throughout the realm but does not employ men of outstanding moral worth, I foresee that when he raises his voice, none will join in harmony, and when he acts, none will accompany him. How few farmers who hire no laborers, or generals who appoint no aides, escape hunger or defeat!

Although employing worthy men is essential for a ruler, worthy men cannot readily be brought into his service. The phoenix of Danshan does not enter an ordinary net; the whale of the blue sea does not take the bait of an ordinary hook. The qilin cannot be tethered, nor can pines and cypresses be confined within a hedge. How, then, could men of moral integrity simply be summoned and made subjects? Thus, rulers who accomplish great things may go to such men and learn from them, or first honor them as teachers and only afterward employ them as ministers. They honor virtue alone, rather than exalted station, and delight in the Way alone, rather than wealth and rank. Only then will those called men of outstanding worth exchange their resolve to dwell among hills and woods for plans to serve at court. When the limbs rejoice, the head is thereby stirred to action: herein lies the means of achieving deeds of unprecedented greatness. When the ears and eyes are clear, the heart and vitals are thereby at ease: herein lies the means of establishing achievements rarely seen in any age. His aspirations are great, unconstrained by what he has seen and heard; his capacity is great, unrestricted by what is immediate and petty. He treats the greatly worthy with ritual respect and employs them—how could he be bound by distinctions of power and rank? Could a ruler’s great accomplishments surpass this? Who but an extraordinary ruler could act thus? If he merely exalts his own exalted position, without knowing to honor virtue, and delights in his own pleasures, without knowing to delight in the Way, such a ruler is certainly unfit to join in great undertakings. Yet if one who cherishes the Way and virtue readily enters his service without waiting for the ruler to show the utmost respect and fulfill every courtesy, how could he too be fit to join in great undertakings?

Thus, what is prized in a ruler is aspiration, and what is prized in a minister is integrity. The ruler who accomplishes great things possesses aspiration; the minister who cannot simply be summoned possesses integrity. One who has aspiration must look to one who has integrity to complete his achievements; one who has integrity must find one who has aspiration to put his cherished principles into practice. When rulers are such men as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, their ministers must be such men as Gao, Kui, Ji, Xie, Yi, and Lü. With a sage ruler and worthy ministers, their great accomplishments cannot be surpassed. From that time onward, those of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties who could be said to have accomplished great things were indeed few. Among the articles of the Grand Pronouncements are “The Merits and Failings of Court Officials,” “Knowing to Repay Kindness and Receiving Blessings,” “Exceeding One’s Station in One’s Dwelling,” and “Do Nothing Wrong.” I have also examined these against the Instructions and Announcements of the Book of Documents. “The Merits and Failings of Court Officials” means precisely “clearly distinguishing whom to demote and whom to promote”; “Knowing to Repay Kindness and Receiving Blessings” means precisely “upon those who do good, blessings descend.” Does not “Exceeding One’s Station in One’s Dwelling” correspond to “Failing to follow the great laws, they thereby draw on evil”? Does not “Do Nothing Wrong” correspond to “the chief evildoers, greatly detested, who bring punishment upon themselves”? Such is the correspondence between what they contain and the Instructions and Announcements.
Emperor Wen, Taizong, produced the book Nature and Principle (Xingli), expanding upon the wellsprings of the transmission of the Way and reviving our flagging cultural tradition. In this book Master Zhou comes first, followed by Master Zhang. For Master Zhou it records the Explanation of the Diagram and the Comprehensive Writings; for Master Zhang, the Western Inscription and Correcting Youthful Ignorance. The Great Declaration speaks of “Heaven having a manifest Way,” of “Heaven and Earth being the parents of the myriad things,” and of “assisting the Lord on High and bringing peace to the four quarters.” How could these fail to accord with the teachings established by Zhou and Zhang in the imperially produced work?

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
四海之風俗而其書則先君道而臣道次
焉君道則重聖德聖學臣道則重輔德經
國也說命所謂從諫則聖所謂念終始典
于學與夫佑烈祖格皇天其與
御製君臣所重之事豈有不同者乎是則
聖作
聖述前輝後映著非常之製作煥至德之文章
誠
大有爲之君貽不世出之典於乎休哉愚也
===
章句竪生草茅賤品是行是訓不識不知
况
天地之大非可以管窺
日月之明非可以螢照執事矜而進焉尚當
以伏羲之卦文王之易大禹之疇畫一爲
明天子
獻
第二問
王寶
punctuated:
四海之風俗，而其書則先君道而臣道次焉。君道則重聖德、聖學，臣道則重輔德、經國也。《說命》所謂「從諫則聖」，所謂「念終始典于學」，與夫「佑烈祖，格皇天」，其與御製君臣所重之事，豈有不同者乎？是則聖作聖述，前輝後映，著非常之製作，煥至德之文章，誠大有爲之君，貽不世出之典。於乎休哉！愚也，章句竪生，草茅賤品，是行是訓，不識不知。况天地之大，非可以管窺；日月之明，非可以螢照。執事矜而進焉，尚當以伏羲之卦、文王之易、大禹之疇，畫一爲明天子獻。

第二問

王寶
translation_en:
…the customs throughout the realm. In this book, the Way of the ruler comes first, followed by the Way of the minister. The Way of the ruler emphasizes sagely virtue and sagely learning; the Way of the minister emphasizes assisting the ruler’s virtue and ordering the state. The statements in “The Charge to Yue”—“Follow remonstrance, and you will become a sage,” “From beginning to end, keep your thoughts constantly on learning,” and “Assist your illustrious ancestor and reach August Heaven”—how could these differ from the matters emphasized for rulers and ministers in the imperially authored work? Thus, sage sovereigns create and transmit: the brilliance of their predecessors is reflected by their successors. They produce extraordinary works and display writings of consummate virtue. Truly, these are sovereigns of great accomplishment, bequeathing canonical works rarely seen in any age. Ah, how splendid!

I, in my ignorance, am but a petty student of textual divisions and phrases, a lowly man of the countryside. I practice these things and follow these teachings, without knowledge or understanding. Moreover, the vastness of Heaven and Earth cannot be viewed through a narrow tube; the radiance of the sun and moon cannot be illuminated by a glowworm. If you, honored officials, take pity on me and advance me, I shall further set out a coherent account of Fuxi’s hexagrams, King Wen’s Changes, and the Great Yu’s categories, to present to the enlightened Son of Heaven.

Second Question

Wang Bao

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭批此篇條荅無遺盖知重
國本而尚友古人者歟
考試官教諭何批忠愛之誠溢於言表可以獻諸
上矣
考試官教諭梁批敷荅詳明髙薦無忝
主器惟長用是立邦家之基錫命以時寔
維為社稷之福三王以來百世不易恭惟
聖天子在上氣鍾乾坤萬古之清淑德起華夷
千載之聽聞大孝孚于
===
兩宮至仁漸於八極
皇天眷命
元子誕生乃者
明詔渙頒
儲嗣寵建布離照於
重光轟震雷於萬里凡有知識孰不鼓舞夫

Associate Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: This essay answers each point without omission. Surely its author understands the importance of the foundation of the state and takes the ancients as his friends.

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:

矣粤稽諸古太甲當幼冲之時得伊尹為

主焉考諸商書所載可知已成王當襁褓

而為有周之賢君焉觀諸賈誼之疏可見
已伊周之事冠冕萬世自時而下東宫之
官之善於輔導者漢有石奮焉孝謹傳家
===
===
聞乎郡國人謂齊魯諸儒自謂弗及夫豈
不宜晉有賀循焉定立制度一時儒宗詔
謂躬訓儲宫默而成化夫豈不當李伯紀
之有疾也太宗賜以步輿引至禁中而問
政焉觀太子弼諧審喻之褒獨無裨於治
道乎魏玄成之已殁也太宗就函得表命
臣書笏而求諫焉觀所言善惡邪正之辨
獨無感於君心乎李適之改官東宫寔見
