title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
曰避賢罷相樂聖銜杯何度量如之魯宗
道任職諭德曾見召於真宗也宗道歸自
肆中但以實告其曰飲酒常情欺君大罪
何忠實如之之數子者在當時雖有可稱
以之而較伊周則相去遠矣方今
明明在上穆穆在下列職
東宮者侍從皆老成之人前後率俊乂之士
輔之必無不至處之必無不周必如易之
養正於蒙而全其正理必如書之習善於
===
初而保其善心浴日于扶桑而畜四海照
臨之象豢龍于淵海而充九霄飛奮之祥
使伊周而在
今日固惟如斯而已愚何贊焉雖然養之不
可不慎望之不可不仁臣子忠愛之情容
有巳乎倘得立
玉堦方寸地則夫志伊尹之所志行周公之
所行而坐漢唐宋諸子於下風固所願也
謹對
punctuated:
曰：「避賢罷相，樂聖銜杯。」何度量如之！魯宗道任職諭德，曾見召於真宗也。宗道歸自肆中，但以實告，其曰：「飲酒常情，欺君大罪。」何忠實如之！之數子者，在當時雖有可稱，以之而較伊周，則相去遠矣。
方今，明明在上，穆穆在下。列職東宮者，侍從皆老成之人，前後率俊乂之士。輔之必無不至，處之必無不周。必如《易》之養正於蒙，而全其正理；必如《書》之習善於初，而保其善心。浴日于扶桑，而畜四海照臨之象；豢龍于淵海，而充九霄飛奮之祥。使伊周而在今日，固惟如斯而已，愚何贊焉？雖然，養之不可不慎，望之不可不仁，臣子忠愛之情容有巳乎？倘得立玉堦方寸地，則夫志伊尹之所志，行周公之所行，而坐漢唐宋諸子於下風，固所願也。謹對。
translation_en:
…said: “Yielding to worthier men, I leave the chief minister’s office; delighting in the ‘sage’—clear wine—I raise my cup.” What magnanimity could equal his! When Lu Zongdao served as Admonisher, he was once summoned by Emperor Zhenzong. Returning from a tavern, Zongdao simply told the truth, saying: “Drinking wine is an ordinary human inclination; deceiving the ruler is a grave crime.” What loyalty and honesty could equal his! These men, though commendable in their own times, fall far short when compared with Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou.
At present, the enlightened sovereign presides above, and reverent ministers serve below. Among those holding posts in the Eastern Palace, the attendants are all mature and experienced men, and those surrounding the heir apparent are outstanding men of talent. Their assistance must leave nothing wanting, and their arrangements must be thorough in every respect. They must, as the Book of Changes teaches, nurture rectitude amid youthful ignorance, preserving his correct moral principles intact; and, as the Book of Documents teaches, cultivate goodness from the beginning, preserving his good heart. They bathe the sun at Fusang, nurturing the promise of its illumination of all within the Four Seas; they rear the dragon in the ocean depths, fostering the auspicious prospect of its soaring through the nine heavens. Were Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou alive today, surely they would do only this. What could an ignorant man like me add? Nevertheless, one must exercise care in nurturing him and benevolence in one’s expectations of him. Could the loyal affection of a subject ever cease? If I might gain even a tiny foothold upon the jade steps of the throne, my wish would indeed be to aspire to what Yi Yin aspired to, to carry out what the Duke of Zhou carried out, and thereby to place the men of the Han, Tang, and Song in an inferior position. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第三問
謝訥
同考試官訓導沈批辯論古人得失其義正而嚴
其詞明而備可取
同考試官教諭强批有考據有折衷佳士也
考試官教諭何批不為問目所窘宜表而出之
考試官教諭梁批策善答
鑑在懸而人之妍媸以别衡在拳而物之
輕重以定盖鑑必自明而后能明諸人衡
===
必自平而后能平諸物埋塵之鑑未星之
衡烏能别妍媸而定輕重哉此人物之賢
否得失必格物窮理者能知之顧愚何人
而足以與此然明問所及不容緘默是故
五服五章天命有德也昔有任銓部者顏
峻毅不可犯於除選之時謝莊歡笑相答
於宣訴之頃故有所謂顏公嗔而與人官
謝公笑而不與人官者然一則過於威厲
欲要孤介之譽一則曲為容納圖止怨謗
punctuated:
第三問
謝訥
同考試官訓導沈批：「辯論古人得失，其義正而嚴，其詞明而備，可取。」
同考試官教諭强批：「有考據，有折衷，佳士也。」
考試官教諭何批：「不為問目所窘，宜表而出之。」
考試官教諭梁批：「策善。」
答：鑑在懸，而人之妍媸以别；衡在拳，而物之輕重以定。盖鑑必自明，而后能明諸人；衡必自平，而后能平諸物。埋塵之鑑、未星之衡，烏能别妍媸而定輕重哉？此人物之賢否得失，必格物窮理者能知之。顧愚何人，而足以與此？然明問所及，不容緘默。是故五服五章，天命有德也。昔有任銓部者，顏峻毅不可犯於除選之時，謝莊歡笑相答於宣訴之頃，故有所謂「顏公嗔而與人官，謝公笑而不與人官」者。然一則過於威厲，欲要孤介之譽；一則曲為容納，圖止怨謗
translation_en:
Third Question
Xie Ne 謝訥
Associate Examiner Shen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “In discussing the merits and failings of men of antiquity, his reasoning is correct and rigorous, and his language clear and comprehensive. Worth selecting.”
Associate Examiner Qiang, Instructor, comments: “He provides documentary evidence and balanced judgments. An excellent scholar.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “He is not constrained by the question’s particulars. He deserves to be singled out for distinction.”
Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “A good policy essay.”
Answer: When a mirror hangs before us, people’s beauty and ugliness can be distinguished; when a balance is held in the hand, things’ lightness and heaviness can be determined. The mirror must itself be clear before it can reveal people clearly; the balance must itself be level before it can weigh things fairly. How could a mirror buried in dust or a balance without graduated markings distinguish beauty from ugliness or determine lightness and heaviness? Thus, only someone who investigates things and exhaustively examines their principles can discern people’s worthiness and unworthiness, their merits and failings. Yet who am I, in my ignorance, to be qualified to undertake this? Nevertheless, since your discerning question addresses these matters, I cannot remain silent.
Thus, the five kinds of ceremonial robes with their five kinds of insignia are Heaven’s means of appointing the virtuous. Among those formerly responsible for personnel selection, Yan was stern and unapproachable when making appointments, while Xie Zhuang responded with laughter and smiles when people presented their appeals. Hence the saying: “Lord Yan scowls but gives people office; Lord Xie smiles but gives people no office.” Yet the former was excessively stern and severe, seeking a reputation for uncompromising integrity; the latter went out of his way to appear accommodating, seeking to put an end to resentment and slander…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之允而揆之正理豈能無議哉五刑五用
天討有罪也昔有任法曹者徐有功直誣
搆之獄活數百家來俊臣用羅織之計破
千餘家故有所謂遇徐必生遇來必死者
然一則專尚仁恕亦無廢職之愆一則過
為慘刻乃有忍心之惡而人之臧否尚何
待辯哉母在敵手徐庶辭先主而卒全其
母焉故程子是之若趙苞之遽戰而殺其
母忠則似矣其如母何友陷無罪左儒諫
===
宣王而卒死於友焉故史臣稱之若酈生
之下齊而欺其友計則行矣其如友何昔
有治單父者子賤任人巫馬期任力任人
為逸而任力為勞其為善政均也昔有用
兵法者孫臏減竈虞詡增竈減竈示弱而
增竈示強其為善戰一也人之才有長有
不長也黃霸之在潁川嘗著循良之譽及
其為相而功名損於治郡此無他才之局
耳人之名有實有不實也殷浩之在江東
punctuated: 之允，而揆之正理，豈能無議哉？五刑五用，天討有罪也。昔有任法曹者，徐有功直誣搆之獄，活數百家；來俊臣用羅織之計，破千餘家。故有所謂「遇徐必生，遇來必死」者。然一則專尚仁恕，亦無廢職之愆；一則過為慘刻，乃有忍心之惡。而人之臧否，尚何待辯哉？母在敵手，徐庶辭先主，而卒全其母焉，故程子是之。若趙苞之遽戰而殺其母，忠則似矣，其如母何？友陷無罪，左儒諫宣王，而卒死於友焉，故史臣稱之。若酈生之下齊而欺其友，計則行矣，其如友何？昔有治單父者，子賤任人，巫馬期任力；任人為逸，而任力為勞，其為善政均也。昔有用兵法者，孫臏減竈，虞詡增竈；減竈示弱，而增竈示強，其為善戰一也。人之才有長有不長也。黃霸之在潁川，嘗著循良之譽；及其為相，而功名損於治郡，此無他，才之局耳。人之名有實有不實也。殷浩之在江東，
translation_en:
…approval [?]; yet, measured against correct principle, how could these actions escape criticism? The five punishments, applied in their five ways, are Heaven’s chastisement of the guilty. Among those who formerly served in judicial offices, Xu Yougong rectified cases involving false accusations and saved several hundred families, while Lai Junchen used schemes of fabricated charges and ruined more than a thousand families. Hence the saying: “Encounter Xu and you will surely live; encounter Lai and you will surely die.” Yet the former, though devoted above all to benevolence and forbearance, committed no fault of neglecting his duties; the latter, excessively cruel and harsh, was guilty of heartlessness. What further argument is needed to distinguish their merits and faults?

When his mother was in enemy hands, Xu Shu took leave of the Former Lord, Liu Bei, and ultimately preserved his mother’s life; Master Cheng therefore approved of him. As for Zhao Bao, who hastily joined battle and thereby caused his mother’s death, his conduct may have resembled loyalty, but what of his mother? When his friend was unjustly accused, Zuo Ru remonstrated with King Xuan and ultimately died for his friend; the historian therefore praised him. As for Master Li’s bringing Qi into submission while deceiving his friend [?], his stratagem may have succeeded, but what of his friend?

Among those who formerly governed Shanfu, Zijian relied on other men, while Wuma Qi relied on his own exertions. Relying on others brought ease, whereas relying on one’s own exertions brought toil; their good government was nonetheless equal. Among those who formerly employed military methods, Sun Bin reduced the number of cooking hearths, while Yu Xu increased them. Reducing the hearths displayed weakness, while increasing them displayed strength; their skill in warfare was nonetheless the same.

People’s abilities have their strengths and their limitations. When Huang Ba was in Yingchuan, he won renown for conscientious and benevolent administration. Once he became Chief Councilor, however, his achievements and reputation fell short of those he had attained in governing a commandery. There was no other reason for this: his abilities were limited in scope. People’s reputations may or may not have substance. When Yin Hao was in Jiangdong…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
嘗渴蒼生之望及其既出而北伐竟無成
功此無他名之浮耳諫官以吐剛為羞則
陽城之沮相裂麻可取矣然在官七年以
此塞責何恠乎論者之預譏士風以不廉
為耻則裴寛之瘞鹿於圃可羡矣然究其
心術有意沽名奚免乎識者之所議夫人
物之賢否得失論固然矣然亦有行高而
被求全之責才劣而遭不虞之褒者故美
玉雖瑕終非碔砆之比良驥雖老豈為駑
===
駘之匹此又秉衡鑑者所當知
第四問
何孟春
同考試官訓導吳批明白通暢
考試官教諭何批援引詳明必該博之士
考試官教諭梁批知先賢出處而善於鋪陳其有
學有志者歟
中州之清淑必有材德生其間此韓公之
格言也山川之秀麗必有俊傑居其間此
punctuated:
嘗渴蒼生之望，及其既出而北伐，竟無成功。此無他，名之浮耳。諫官以吐剛為羞，則陽城之沮相裂麻可取矣；然在官七年，以此塞責，何恠乎論者之預譏？士風以不廉為耻，則裴寛之瘞鹿於圃可羡矣；然究其心術，有意沽名，奚免乎識者之所議？夫人物之賢否、得失，論固然矣；然亦有行高而被求全之責，才劣而遭不虞之褒者。故美玉雖瑕，終非碔砆之比；良驥雖老，豈為駑駘之匹？此又秉衡鑑者所當知。
第四問
何孟春
同考試官訓導吳批：明白通暢。
考試官教諭何批：援引詳明，必該博之士。
考試官教諭梁批：知先賢出處，而善於鋪陳，其有學有志者歟！
中州之清淑，必有材德生其間，此韓公之格言也；山川之秀麗，必有俊傑居其間，此
translation_en:
…once bore the hopes of the common people [?]; yet after he entered public service and undertook a northern expedition, he achieved no success. This was simply because his reputation lacked substance. If a remonstrance official considers it shameful to shrink before the powerful, then Yang Cheng’s opposition to a chief councillor’s appointment and his tearing up the appointment edict deserve approval. Yet, having held office for seven years, he discharged his responsibility with this alone: why be surprised that commentators had already criticized him? If the ethos of scholars treats a lack of integrity as shameful, then Pei Kuan’s burial of a deer in his garden deserves admiration. Yet, when his motives are examined, he intended to purchase a reputation: how could he escape the criticism of discerning observers? Such judgments of people’s worth and shortcomings, successes and failures, are certainly sound. Yet there are also those whose conduct is lofty but who are censured for falling short of perfection, and those of inferior ability who receive unexpected praise. Thus, even flawed fine jade is never comparable to an ordinary stone resembling jade; and how could a fine steed, though old, be ranked with inferior horses? This, too, is something those charged with weighing and assessing people ought to understand.
Fourth Question
He Mengchun
Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: Clear, lucid, and fluent.
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: The citations are detailed and clear. He must be a man of extensive learning.
Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: He understands when the worthies of earlier times entered service or withdrew, and is skilled in exposition. Surely he possesses both learning and aspiration!
Where Zhongzhou’s vital influences are pure and harmonious, men of talent and virtue must be born among them: this is Master Han’s maxim. Where mountains and rivers are beautiful, outstanding men must dwell among them: this is…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
歐公之確論也以韓歐之言而徵諸吾鄉
之先達以先達之賢而驗諸山川之靈異
則執事之間可復而先達之果由於山川
也信矣濂溪周子雖築居廬山然世家營
道以生默契道體不由師傅
聖朝爲之立祠營道而官其子孫焉二程夫子
雖派系河南然父尉黃陂以生受學濂溪
充然有得宋人爲之立坊黃陂而思其父
子焉胡文定之在衡山嘗與張南軒講學
===
而春秋之旨大明學春秋者宗之張南軒
之居湘潭又與朱晦菴講學而義利之辨
甚嚴談義利者主之隆中今在襄陽也諸
葛亮高卧之所其起於漢昭烈之三顧也
乃爲出師二表以上焉先民獨謂忠貫日
星表裏訓命然其氣之正也孰當浯溪今
在祁陽也元次山居官之所其喜夫唐肅
宗之即位也乃作中興一頌以美焉先民
雖謂背父擅立適爲罪狀然其文之壯也
punctuated: 歐公之確論也。以韓歐之言而徵諸吾鄉之先達，以先達之賢而驗諸山川之靈異，則執事之間可復，而先達之果由於山川也信矣。濂溪周子雖築居廬山，然世家營道以生，默契道體，不由師傅。聖朝爲之立祠營道，而官其子孫焉。二程夫子雖派系河南，然父尉黃陂以生，受學濂溪，充然有得。宋人爲之立坊黃陂，而思其父子焉。胡文定之在衡山，嘗與張南軒講學，而春秋之旨大明，學春秋者宗之。張南軒之居湘潭，又與朱晦菴講學，而義利之辨甚嚴，談義利者主之。隆中今在襄陽也，諸葛亮高卧之所。其起於漢昭烈之三顧也，乃爲出師二表以上焉。先民獨謂忠貫日星，表裏訓命，然其氣之正也，孰當？浯溪今在祁陽也，元次山居官之所。其喜夫唐肅宗之即位也，乃作中興一頌以美焉。先民雖謂背父擅立，適爲罪狀，然其文之壯也，
translation_en:
…was Lord Ouyang’s firm judgment. If we test the words of Han and Ouyang against the eminent predecessors of our own region, and use those predecessors’ worthiness to verify the wondrous spiritual potency of its mountains and rivers, then your question [?] can be answered, and we may indeed be certain that these predecessors owed their emergence to the mountains and rivers. Although Master Zhou Lianxi built his dwelling at Lushan, his family had lived for generations at Yingdao, where he was born. He tacitly apprehended the substance of the Way without instruction from a teacher. Our sagely dynasty established a shrine to him at Yingdao and granted office to his descendants. Although the two Masters Cheng traced their lineage to Henan, they were born while their father served as district defender of Huangpi. They studied under Lianxi and attained a rich understanding. People of the Song erected a commemorative gateway for them at Huangpi and cherished the memory of father and sons alike. While living at Hengshan, Hu Wending once discussed learning with Zhang Nanxuan [?], greatly elucidating the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals; students of that classic took him as their master. While living at Xiangtan, Zhang Nanxuan also discussed learning with Zhu Hui’an, drawing an exceedingly strict distinction between righteousness and profit; those who discussed righteousness and profit took him as their authority.

Longzhong, now in Xiangyang, was the place where Zhuge Liang lived in retirement. When he emerged in response to the three visits of Emperor Zhaolie of Han, he composed and submitted his two Memorials on Sending Forth the Army. Earlier men declared that his loyalty shone through sun and stars, and that these memorials accorded inwardly and outwardly with the Instructions and Charges of the Book of Documents. Indeed, who could rival the rectitude of his spirit? Wuxi, now in Qiyang, was the place where Yuan Cishan held office. Rejoicing at the accession of Emperor Suzong of Tang, he composed an Ode to the Restoration in praise of it. Although earlier men said that Suzong had turned against his father and assumed the throne without authorization, so that the ode amounted instead to an indictment of his crimes, yet, as for the grandeur of its writing …

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
孰與屈原事楚懷王靳尚諧而疎之作離
騷賦以自況其怨也怨其不得於君也伯
奇事父吉甫後母讒而逐之作履霜操以
自傷其悲也悲其不得於親也之數君子
或以道德顯或以文章名或以功業著或
以忠節聞蓋山川毓秀豪傑挺生非湖湘
之士天下之士也非一時之才百世之才
也愚也高山仰止景行行止久矣執事與
其進竊有志焉
===
第五問
楊猇
同考試官訓導閔批灼有定見舉而措之沛然矣
同考試官學正侯批重於得人其識時務之俊傑歟
考試官教諭何批議論鑿鑿可用令人起敬
考試官教諭梁批深知救時之急務
論事非難任事惟難任事非難任人惟難
故時事之難處非所患而任事之得人在
所患苟得人任事則隨事收功夫復何難
punctuated:
孰與？屈原事楚懷王，靳尚諧而疎之，作《離騷賦》以自況。其怨也，怨其不得於君也。伯奇事父吉甫，後母讒而逐之，作《履霜操》以自傷。其悲也，悲其不得於親也。之數君子，或以道德顯，或以文章名，或以功業著，或以忠節聞。蓋山川毓秀，豪傑挺生，非湖湘之士，天下之士也；非一時之才，百世之才也。愚也「高山仰止，景行行止」久矣。執事與其進，竊有志焉。

第五問
楊猇
同考試官訓導閔批：灼有定見，舉而措之，沛然矣。
同考試官學正侯批：重於得人，其識時務之俊傑歟！
考試官教諭何批：議論鑿鑿可用，令人起敬。
考試官教諭梁批：深知救時之急務。

論事非難，任事惟難；任事非難，任人惟難。故時事之難處非所患，而任事之得人在所患。苟得人任事，則隨事收功，夫復何難
translation_en:
…who could compare with him? Qu Yuan served King Huai of Chu, but Jin Shang spoke against him [?], causing the king to estrange him. He composed the Rhapsody on Encountering Sorrow (Li sao) to portray his own circumstances. His resentment arose from his failure to gain his ruler’s favor. Boqi served his father Jifu, but his stepmother slandered him and had him driven out. He composed the Lament on Treading Frost (Lüshuang cao) to mourn his plight. His sorrow arose from his failure to gain his parent’s affection. These gentlemen were distinguished variously for moral virtue, literary composition, achievements in service, or loyal integrity. The mountains and rivers nurtured their exceptional qualities, and outstanding men arose. They were men not merely of Huxiang, but of all the realm; talents not merely of one age, but of a hundred generations. I have long felt toward them as in the lines, “I look up to the lofty mountain; I follow the great road.” Since you, sir, encourage advancement, I humbly aspire to follow them.

Fifth Question
Yang Xiao
Associate Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He clearly has firm judgments. Put them into practice, and their efficacy will be abundant.”
Associate Examiner Hou, Instructor, comments: “He lays emphasis on obtaining the right men. Is he not an outstanding talent who understands the affairs of the times?”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “His arguments are precise and practicable, inspiring respect.”
Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “He deeply understands the urgent tasks necessary to remedy the troubles of the times.”

Discussing affairs is not difficult; taking responsibility for them is difficult. Taking responsibility for affairs is not difficult; appointing the right men is difficult. Thus, what warrants concern is not the difficulty of managing current affairs, but whether the right men can be found to undertake them. If the right men are found to undertake affairs, success will follow in each case. What difficulty would then remain…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
哉執事以時務之切於湖藩者爲問盖因
愚所知者示之也請以得人爲明問復可
乎嗟乎老醫一匕危病立痊善奕一着敗
枰坐勝得人故也兹湖藩之可患者多矣
而其所從來者尚矣然非得人安能變其
故而新之哉夫以災荒言之湖民往歲乾
旱填餓殍於溝壑今年水溢沉廬舍於深
淵疲則甚矣立視其死奚忍哉必施賑恤
之典寬賦役之征得人如朱元晦之在浙
===
東而活人以數萬也如范仲淹之在江淮
而招商以貿易也庶其有濟乎以風俗言
之湖民尚鬼好遊爭徼福於淫祠勁悍獷
夷傳箕裘於弓弩習則敝矣坐視其陋奚
可哉必嚴左道之禁重禮義之俗得人如
陳襄之在仙居立約以教民也如文翁之
在西蜀興學以勸士也庶其可正乎流移
以江漢為居止而農賈靡定鴻鴈無安集
之期雞犬失孕字之候豈無屯結之可畏
punctuated:
哉！執事以時務之切於湖藩者爲問，盖因愚所知者示之也。請以得人爲明問復，可乎？嗟乎！老醫一匕，危病立痊；善奕一着，敗枰坐勝：得人故也。兹湖藩之可患者多矣，而其所從來者尚矣。然非得人，安能變其故而新之哉？
夫以災荒言之，湖民往歲乾旱，填餓殍於溝壑；今年水溢，沉廬舍於深淵。疲則甚矣，立視其死，奚忍哉？必施賑恤之典，寬賦役之征，得人如朱元晦之在浙東，而活人以數萬也；如范仲淹之在江淮，而招商以貿易也。庶其有濟乎！
以風俗言之，湖民尚鬼好遊，爭徼福於淫祠；勁悍獷夷，傳箕裘於弓弩。習則敝矣，坐視其陋，奚可哉？必嚴左道之禁，重禮義之俗，得人如陳襄之在仙居，立約以教民也；如文翁之在西蜀，興學以勸士也。庶其可正乎！
流移以江漢為居止，而農賈靡定；鴻鴈無安集之期，雞犬失孕字之候。豈無屯結之可畏
translation_en:
…what difficulty could there be! You, sir, have asked about current affairs of pressing concern to Huguang, presumably presenting your question in terms of what I, in my ignorance, might know. May I reply to your discerning question by discussing the securing of capable men? Alas! One spoonful from an experienced physician immediately cures a dangerous illness; one move by a skilled player turns a losing board into victory. This is because the right person has been found. There are now many grounds for concern in Huguang, and their origins reach far back. Yet without capable men, how can its old ways be changed and renewed?
Consider famine and natural disaster. In past years, drought in Huguang left the bodies of the starved filling ditches and ravines; this year, overflowing waters have submerged homes in deep floods. The people are utterly exhausted. How could one bear to stand by and watch them die? We must implement measures of famine relief and ease the levying of taxes and labor services. We must secure men like Zhu Yuanhui, who saved tens of thousands of lives while serving in eastern Zhejiang, or Fan Zhongyan, who attracted merchants to trade while serving in the Jiang-Huai region. Then perhaps relief could be achieved!
Consider customs. The people of Huguang revere spirits and delight in roaming about, vying to seek blessings at unauthorized shrines; the fierce and unruly non-Han peoples pass down skill with bows and crossbows as their hereditary occupation. Their habits have become corrupt. How could one simply sit by and watch their debasement? We must strictly enforce prohibitions against heterodox practices and give greater weight to customs of ritual propriety and righteousness. We must secure men like Chen Xiang, who established covenants to instruct the people while serving in Xianju, or Wen Weng, who founded schools to encourage scholars while serving in western Shu. Then perhaps these customs could be set right!
Displaced people make their homes in the Jiang-Han region, yet have no settled livelihood in farming or trade. Like wild geese, they have no prospect of settling peacefully; even their chickens and dogs miss the seasons for breeding and rearing young. Is there no reason to fear their gathering into bands…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
乎殆必各因久近或占籍或遣還得人如
富弼之在青州隨遠近而給歸糧則居民
按堵之樂可期矣賊盜以荆衡為淵藪而
剽竊靡常虎狼有入室之虞狐䑕肆嚙噬
之計豈無嘯聚之可憂乎殆必嚴立保伍
或聯捕或分督得人如龔遂之在渤海賣
刀劒而買牛犢則路不拾遺之效可臻矣
武昌漢陽之東西相峙一省都會之衝莫
先焉以兵戎言之武昌數不滿萬而漢陽
===
數不及千能無防禦不及之慮耶但戎籍
已定事難驟更要在選統領之官于以嚴
操練之法優糧賞之頒而私役者痛革焉
必得人如韓琦之領兵事而賊聞膽寒可
也寓兵於農何必拘拘於古制哉德安安
陸之
王府並建一時營繕之舉莫煩焉以工費言
之德安動以萬計而安陸不止數千能無
日計不足之嘆耶但
punctuated:
乎？殆必各因久近，或占籍，或遣還，得人如富弼之在青州，隨遠近而給歸糧，則居民按堵之樂可期矣。
賊盜以荆衡為淵藪，而剽竊靡常，虎狼有入室之虞，狐䑕肆嚙噬之計，豈無嘯聚之可憂乎？殆必嚴立保伍，或聯捕，或分督，得人如龔遂之在渤海，賣刀劒而買牛犢，則路不拾遺之效可臻矣。
武昌、漢陽之東西相峙，一省都會之衝莫先焉。以兵戎言之，武昌數不滿萬，而漢陽數不及千，能無防禦不及之慮耶？但戎籍已定，事難驟更，要在選統領之官，于以嚴操練之法，優糧賞之頒，而私役者痛革焉。必得人如韓琦之領兵事，而賊聞膽寒可也。寓兵於農，何必拘拘於古制哉？
德安、安陸之王府並建，一時營繕之舉莫煩焉。以工費言之，德安動以萬計，而安陸不止數千，能無日計不足之嘆耶？但
translation_en:
…? Surely the measures must take account of how long each has been there: some should be entered in the local registers, while others should be sent home. If we obtain someone like Fu Bi in Qingzhou, who provided grain for the journey home according to the distance, we may expect the inhabitants to enjoy living peacefully in their homes.
Bandits and thieves make Jing and Heng their strongholds, plundering and stealing unpredictably. There is the danger of tigers and wolves entering people’s houses, while foxes and rats freely pursue their schemes of gnawing and devouring. How could their gathering into bands not be cause for concern? Surely we must rigorously establish mutual-responsibility groups, either coordinating pursuit and arrest or assigning separate supervisory responsibilities. If we obtain someone like Gong Sui in Bohai, who induced people to sell their swords and buy cattle and calves, we can achieve a state in which no one pockets property lost on the roads.
Wuchang and Hanyang face one another to east and west; no other metropolitan centers in the province surpass them in strategic importance. As for military strength, Wuchang has fewer than ten thousand troops, and Hanyang fewer than one thousand. How could there be no concern that their defenses will prove inadequate? Yet the military registers are already fixed, and arrangements cannot easily be changed abruptly. The essential thing is to select officers to command them, thereby enforcing rigorous methods of training, providing generous grain allowances and rewards, and thoroughly abolishing the use of soldiers for private service. We must obtain someone like Han Qi in command of military affairs, whose very reputation struck terror into the bandits. With soldiers incorporated among the farmers, why need we cling so rigidly to ancient institutions?
The princely residences at De’an and Anlu are being built simultaneously; no other construction undertaking of the time is more burdensome. As for construction expenses, those at De’an readily run into tens of thousands, while those at Anlu exceed several thousand. How could there be no lament that the daily reckoning shows insufficient funds? Yet…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
藩封攸繫事非得已要在重督理之官于以
嚴考覈之程謹費出之度而過侈者弗為
焉必得人如劉晏之領度支而以羨補乏
可也榷筭征商何必屑屑於民利哉以非
為是以曲為直而噓灰鼓燄者爭鬭之風
日長刁頑何其多然使民無訟理之正也
但庶頑未可以易感今使為司牧者公以
為明廉以為威如子路之片言折獄如曾
子之哀矜勿喜夫何獄訟之弗清而患其
===
===
蝟興乎以强凌弱以衆暴寡而狼子野心
者攻殺之患相尋蠻酋何其肆然聲罪致
討法之正也但小醜未足以加兵今使帥
邊城者懷之以恩懾之以威如趙充國之
在金城如郭子儀之在涇陽夫何豪强之
弗服而患其狠拒乎愚非伯樂也烏足以
知良馬非公輸也烏足以識良材姑摭拾
以對然騏驥脫塩車之厄而樟楠充廊廟
之用則有望於賢執事也
punctuated:
藩封攸繫，事非得已。要在重督理之官，于以嚴考覈之程，謹費出之度，而過侈者弗為焉。必得人如劉晏之領度支，而以羨補乏，可也。榷筭征商，何必屑屑於民利哉？
以非為是，以曲為直，而噓灰鼓燄者，爭鬭之風日長，刁頑何其多！然使民無訟，理之正也。但庶頑未可以易感，今使為司牧者，公以為明，廉以為威，如子路之片言折獄，如曾子之哀矜勿喜，夫何獄訟之弗清，而患其蝟興乎？
以强凌弱，以衆暴寡，而狼子野心者，攻殺之患相尋，蠻酋何其肆！然聲罪致討，法之正也。但小醜未足以加兵，今使帥邊城者，懷之以恩，懾之以威，如趙充國之在金城，如郭子儀之在涇陽，夫何豪强之弗服，而患其狠拒乎？
愚非伯樂也，烏足以知良馬？非公輸也，烏足以識良材？姑摭拾以對。然騏驥脫塩車之厄，而樟楠充廊廟之用，則有望於賢執事也。
translation_en:
…the establishment of princely fiefs is at stake, and the undertaking cannot be avoided. The essential thing is to give due weight to the officials supervising the work, enforce rigorous procedures for evaluating performance, carefully regulate expenditure, and refrain from excessive extravagance. We must obtain men like Liu Yan when he managed state expenditure, using surpluses to make up deficiencies; that would suffice. Why resort to monopoly levies and taxes on merchants, quibbling over the people's profits?
There are those who take wrong for right and crookedness for uprightness, blowing upon ashes and fanning flames. The habit of quarrelling and fighting grows daily: how numerous are the crafty and refractory! Yet bringing the people to have no litigation is the proper ideal of governance. But the refractory multitude cannot readily be moved to reform. If those who shepherd the people now derived their discernment from impartiality and their authority from incorruptibility, deciding cases with a single word like Zilu, and showing sorrow and compassion rather than delight like Zengzi, what lawsuits would remain unsettled? Why then fear their springing up like a hedgehog's spines?
There are those who use strength to bully the weak and numbers to oppress the few, with the savage hearts of wolf cubs. Attacks and killings follow one upon another: how unrestrained are the non-Han chieftains! To proclaim their crimes and punish them is indeed the proper course under the law. Yet these petty miscreants do not warrant deploying troops. If those commanding frontier cities now won them over through kindness and overawed them through authority, like Zhao Chongguo at Jincheng and Guo Ziyi at Jingyang, what powerful local bullies would fail to submit? Why then fear their fierce resistance?
I, in my ignorance, am no Bole: how could I be competent to recognize fine horses? I am no Gongshu: how could I be competent to identify fine timber? I have merely gathered these observations to offer a reply. Yet for thoroughbreds to escape the hardship of hauling salt carts, and for camphor and nanmu timber to find use in the halls of government, I place my hopes in you, worthy officials.

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
弘治壬子湖廣鄉試巡按監
察御史汪宗器暨藩臬提調
監試諸執事惟公惟慎遵例
取士若干刻其文之優者若
干將錄以
進昌謹序其後曰元氣在天地
===
發於人爲文元氣之盛衰而
文寔乘之故有治世之音有
亂世之音氣之盛衰徵於世
有吉人之言有凶人之言氣
之盛衰徵於人文之繫于元
氣有以哉三代而上文以時
異元氣噩如也自漢而下互
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

弘治壬子，湖廣鄉試，巡按監察御史汪宗器暨藩臬提調、監試諸執事，惟公惟慎，遵例取士若干，刻其文之優者若干，將錄以進。昌謹序其後曰：元氣在天地，發於人爲文。元氣之盛衰，而文寔乘之，故有治世之音，有亂世之音，氣之盛衰徵於世；有吉人之言，有凶人之言，氣之盛衰徵於人。文之繫于元氣，有以哉！三代而上，文以時異，元氣噩如也。自漢而下，互
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the renzi year of Hongzhi [1492], at the Huguang Provincial Examination, Wang Zongqi 汪宗器, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector, together with the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions serving as Proctors and examination monitors, acted with impartiality and care. Following established regulations, they selected a certain number of candidates and had a selection of their superior compositions engraved for printing, intending to submit the record to the throne. I, Chang 昌, respectfully append this postface:

Primal vital energy resides in Heaven and Earth; expressed through human beings, it becomes writing. Writing indeed follows the flourishing and decline of this energy. Thus there are the sounds of an orderly age and those of a disordered age: the flourishing and decline of this energy are manifest in the world. There are the words of good people and those of evil people: the flourishing and decline of this energy are manifest in individuals. There is indeed a reason for writing’s connection with primal vital energy! In the Three Dynasties and earlier, writing differed with the times, but primal vital energy remained lofty and austere. From the Han onward, there was an alternation …

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
爲醇疵固元氣升降乎其中
爾我
朝酌古爲治養元氣於斯文洪
武永樂間雖棘屋之文恢恢
古度元氣盛不可當厥後寢
涉華靡甚至論範錦綉策諸
書傳焉文習幾趨於陋元氣
===
嘗少損矣比年作者甫嚮初
轍適遇
聖天子紹統之明年鄉試又明年
會試諸錄舉黜浮就實粹然
温厚之詞學者翕然崇尚今
歲復當大比群湖湘士而三
試之文多典雅絕無險陂淫
punctuated: 爲醇疵，固元氣升降乎其中爾。我朝酌古爲治，養元氣於斯文。洪武、永樂間，雖棘屋之文，恢恢古度，元氣盛不可當。厥後寢涉華靡，甚至《論範》《錦綉策》諸書傳焉，文習幾趨於陋，元氣嘗少損矣。比年作者甫嚮初轍，適遇聖天子紹統之明年鄉試，又明年會試，諸錄舉黜浮就實，粹然温厚之詞，學者翕然崇尚。今歲復當大比，群湖湘士，而三試之文多典雅，絕無險陂淫
translation_en:
…between purity and defect: surely this was simply the primordial vital force rising and falling within it. Our dynasty drew upon antiquity in governing and nurtured that vital force through literary culture. During the Hongwu and Yongle reigns, even writings produced within the thorn-enclosed examination compounds displayed the expansive measure of antiquity; their vital force flourished irresistibly. Thereafter, writing gradually drifted toward ornate extravagance. Books such as Models of Discourses (Lunfan) and Brocade Policy Essays (Jinxiu ce) even circulated, and literary practice nearly descended into vulgarity. The vital force did for a time suffer some diminution.

In recent years, writers had only just begun to return to the original path when the Provincial Examination took place in the year after the sagely Son of Heaven succeeded to the throne, followed the next year by the Metropolitan Examination. The examination records all rejected superficiality in favor of substance, presenting language of unalloyed gentleness and generosity, which scholars unanimously came to esteem. This year the triennial examination again fell due, bringing together the scholars of Huxiang. Their writings in the three sessions were mostly classical and elegant, entirely free of tendencies toward the tortuous, the deviant, and the licentious…

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
蕩之偏如額取上春官者尤
為翹楚治世之音吉人之言
也嗚呼元氣盛矣哉夫元氣
猶水也文舟也水勢壯則舟
雄而速弱則委以滯焉舟之
通塞不乗水之盛衰乎然則
文之大昌于
===
今日者寔元氣攸充所謂水漲
舟行更無着力處莫之為而
為者矣書曰天惟純佑命則
商實詩曰思皇多士生此王
國兹維其時諸君子尚相與
勉力以永我
國家元氣於億萬斯年乎
punctuated: 蕩之偏。如額取上春官者，尤為翹楚，治世之音，吉人之言也。嗚呼，元氣盛矣哉！夫元氣猶水也，文舟也。水勢壯，則舟雄而速；弱，則委以滯焉。舟之通塞，不乗水之盛衰乎？然則文之大昌于今日者，寔元氣攸充。所謂「水漲舟行，更無着力處」，莫之為而為者矣。《書》曰：「天惟純佑命，則商實。」《詩》曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。」兹維其時，諸君子尚相與勉力，以永我國家元氣於億萬斯年乎？
translation_en:
…the excesses of licentiousness. Those selected within the prescribed quota to proceed to the Ministry of Rites are especially outstanding. Their writings are the sounds of an age of good government, the words of worthy men. Ah, how abundant is the vital force!

Vital force is like water, and writing is like a boat. When the water flows strongly, the boat moves powerfully and swiftly; when it flows weakly, the boat languishes and stalls. Does not the boat’s progress or obstruction depend upon the water’s rise and fall? Thus, the great flourishing of writing today truly comes from the fullness of this vital force. As the saying goes, “When the water rises, the boat moves; no further exertion is needed.” It happens without anyone making it happen.

The Book of Documents says, “Heaven bestowed its full favor and mandate; thus Shang was filled with worthy men.” The Book of Odes says, “How splendid are the many men of talent, born in this royal realm!” Now indeed is such a time. Will you gentlemen not strive together to perpetuate our state’s vital force for countless millions of years?

title: 弘治五年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
直隸寧國府南陵縣儒學教
諭何昌謹序
